item.title: Abia picked for regional stroke, neurovascular centre
item.description: . As Otti govt secures int’l recognition for health reforms By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State has emerged as the preferred location for a proposed stroke and neurovascular centre to serve Nigeria and West Africa, following its participation in the 2026 Sweden-Africa Neurosurgery Symposium in Gothenburg, Sweden. The state Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this while briefing newsmen on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Alex Otti at Government House, Umuahia. Kanu said the selection was in recognition of Abia’s strides in healthcare delivery and the availability of qualified medical specialists, describing it as another milestone in the state’s ongoing health sector reforms. He said the proposed centre would address the rising incidence of stroke across Africa, particularly Nigeria, by providing specialised facilities for comprehensive treatment and management of neurovascular conditions. According to him, the state government had approved the participation of the Ministry of Health in the international symposium to explore strategic partnerships and opportunities for specialised healthcare development. The Commissioner said Abia’s health sector reforms were also showcased at the symposium, adding that the Ministry of Health had recently been recognised as a national self-care champion. He said the recognition underscored the state’s growing capacity to promote preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyles among residents. On public health preparedness, Kanu disclosed that the government had established a multi-sectoral frontline technical working group to strengthen emergency response mechanisms. He said the group had developed an Ebola preparedness and response plan, while the government had expanded the deployment of modern medical technology in specialised healthcare. Kanu further disclosed that the Infectious Disease Hospital in Aba had been completed, alongside an infectious disease facility and specialist hospital in Umuahia, as part of efforts to strengthen the state’s capacity to tackle Ebola and other infectious diseases. item.content:encoded: . As Otti govt secures int’l recognition for health reforms By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State has emerged as the preferred location for a proposed stroke and neurovascular centre to serve Nigeria and West Africa, following its participation in the 2026 Sweden-Africa Neurosurgery Symposium in Gothenburg, Sweden. The state Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this while briefing newsmen on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Alex Otti at Government House, Umuahia. Kanu said the selection was in recognition of Abia’s strides in healthcare delivery and the availability of qualified medical specialists, describing it as another milestone in the state’s ongoing health sector reforms. He said the proposed centre would address the rising incidence of stroke across Africa, particularly Nigeria, by providing specialised facilities for comprehensive treatment and management of neurovascular conditions. According to him, the state government had approved the participation of the Ministry of Health in the international symposium to explore strategic partnerships and opportunities for specialised healthcare development. The Commissioner said Abia’s health sector reforms were also showcased at the symposium, adding that the Ministry of Health had recently been recognised as a national self-care champion. He said the recognition underscored the state’s growing capacity to promote preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyles among residents. On public health preparedness, Kanu disclosed that the government had established a multi-sectoral frontline technical working group to strengthen emergency response mechanisms. He said the group had developed an Ebola preparedness and response plan, while the government had expanded the deployment of modern medical technology in specialised healthcare. Kanu further disclosed that the Infectious Disease Hospital in Aba had been completed, alongside an infectious disease facility and specialist hospital in Umuahia, as part of efforts to strengthen the state’s capacity to tackle Ebola and other infectious diseases. He, however, said no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera or avian influenza were recorded in Abia. The Commissioner also announced progress in the agricultural intervention programme being implemented across the state’s 17 local government areas in partnership with the councils. He said the initiative was designed to attract investments, boost food production, develop viable agricultural enterprises and create employment through strengthened agricultural value chains. The Commissioner disclosed that Arochukwu LGA had a plantation plantation of over 86,000 trees, describing it as highly commendable. On housing, Kanu said the government’s residential development at Pocket Layout had attracted overwhelming interest, with applications exceeding available units. He disclosed that the government was considering a lottery system to ensure fairness, transparency and equity in allocating the houses. Responding to questions, the Commissioner for Housing, Architect Chiemela Uzoije, said the project had been oversubscribed, with more than 530 applications received for 173 housing units. “We have a total of 173 units of residences coming up there, but at the last count, up to 530-something have applied. “It is not going to be what it used to be in the past. It is going to be in a very free and transparent manner,” Uzoije said. Kanu also disclosed that a comprehensive assessment of existing housing estates and layouts was underway to identify infrastructure gaps and prioritise government intervention. He said the exercise would address deficits in internal roads, utilities, security infrastructure and other essential facilities needed to improve living conditions in the estates. On abandoned federal housing projects, the Governor’s Special Adviser, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma, urged the media to hold public officials accountable, particularly over projects initiated by the Federal Government but left uncompleted. Ekeoma said the Abia State Government had been executing some federal projects, stressing that providing land and fulfilling other fundamental requirements remained critical to their implementation. item.title: “There’s been good conversations…”: Harry Kane provides key future update amid Man United links
item.description: “There’s been good conversations…”: Harry Kane provides key future update amid Man United links Manchester United may be desperate to sign a proven striker in 2027, but it now appears that one of their priority targets is all but out of reach. The Red Devils’ sufferings this season can be traced to their inability to bolster the attack over the summer. The Premier League giants were scoring goals for fun last campaign after Michael Carrick’s arrival. Benjamin Sesko was very impressive until his unfortunate injury in the final weeks of the season, while Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo enjoyed solid debut campaigns at Old Trafford as well. However, there was a belief that their relaxed schedule – having played one game a week as they were only involved in the Premier League – helped their cause. United eventually secured third place in the league and the general belief was that they would struggle with the rigours of Champions League football. As such, attacking reinforcements were expected before the start of the season, especially a new striker to compete with Sesko given Joshua Zirkzee’s poor form. Among the candidates linked with United for the job was Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane. United long-term admirers of Harry Kane United have had their eyes on Kane since his time with Tottenham Hotspur, and spurned the chance to secure his services in the summer of 2023. The Englishman ended up joining Bayern Munich instead, and has been a revelation at the Allianz Arena. Kane’s exploits with the Bundesliga champions has seen him lift the 2026 Ballon d’Or. The Red Devils will be ruing the decision to opt for Rasmus Hojlund instead of the 33-year-old, because goalscoring remains the team’s bane right now. The Premier League giants have created chances this season, but have lacked a world-class finisher in the team. United need someone who can keep the opposition on their toes and help bring their speedy runners into the game. There is no one better than Kane for the job at the moment, and because his contract with the Bavarians expires next summer, it was believed that United could have a chance to rectify their previous error in 2027. However, the Englishman has now provided a timely update on his future that is likely to pour cold water on the Red Devils’ plans. Kane set for Bayern Munich stay Kane has previously revealed that he is in renewal talks with the German giants. Speaking to the press in the build-up to the Champions League game against Atletico Madrid, the player confirmed that he is very close to committing his future at the Allianz Arena. The English striker said: “I’d say it’s [a] matter of days. There’s been good conversations over this weekend and today as well. I know I keep saying we’re close, but we are extremely close now.” The update will be a big blow for the Red Devils, who desperately need a proven No. 9 in January to get their season back on track. The English giants are 17th in the Premier League table after nine games this season

The proposed January arrival of someone like Kane would have vastly improved the attack, but it now appears that INEOS will have to look elsewhere to address their goalscoring woes.

item.title: West Ham sack head coach Nuno Espirito Santo
item.description: Nuno Espirito Santo took charge of West Ham in September 2025 [Shutterstock] West Ham United have sacked head coach Nuno Espirito Santo after their disappointing start to the Championship season. The 52-year-old has been in charge since September 2025 and oversaw the Hammers' relegation from the Premier League last season. Widely seen as favourites for automatic promotion, the London side are currently eighth in the table, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough. They have won two of their last six games and have lost back-to-back home matches - going down 3-2 to Southampton and then 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday - losses that have seen them drop down from second place. Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also left the club. Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of the side for their Championship trip to Cardiff City on Wednesday night. "Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club's objectives and expectations remain on track," a West Ham United statement read. "West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future. "The process of recruiting a new head coach is already under way." West Ham appoint Nuno after sacking Potter What happens now at relegated West Ham? The decision means West Ham are looking for their fourth permanent manager since David Moyes left the London Stadium in May 2024. His successor Julen Lopetegui was sacked after just six months in charge with the Hammers mid-table having won six of their 20 Premier League matches. He was replaced by former Chelsea and Brighton boss Graham Potter, who oversaw a 14th-placed finish, but was sacked after only eight months in charge with the club 19th in the table. The club opted to stick with former Wolves and Tottenham Hotspur boss Espirito Santo despite him being unable to turn around the club's fortunes. They were relegated at the end of last season after finishing two points behind Spurs. This season had a troubled start for the Hammers - they failed to win any of their first three league matches and were 19th in the table. But a run of four successive wins in the first half of September, where they scored 16 goals and went top of the table, appeared to show they had adapted to the second tier, with a 6-0 win over Wrexham the highlight of the run. But just two league victories have come since - a 6-0 win at nine-man Lincoln City and a 1-0 victory at Swansea City came after draws with London rivals Millwall and QPR. item.title: Raspberry Pi hikes prices again, barely a month after the last round
item.description: Raspberry Pi has announced yet another round of price hikes, this time adding $80 to the cost of its 16GB Pi 5, which now sells for more than three times its original launch price. The latest bump, announced by Raspberry Pi boss Eben Upton, takes the 16GB Pi 5 to a whopping $385. The 16GB Compute Module 5 variants are also getting $40 more expensive, although the Raspberry Pi 500+, which packs the same amount of RAM, has escaped this particular round. Upton blamed a familiar culprit: soaring memory costs, worsened by a lack of alternative suppliers for 16GB DRAM and ongoing shortages of other components. "Unfortunately, a lack of alternative supply for 16GB DRAM, compounded by other ongoing component shortages, means we now need to make further price increases on some of our highest-density products," Upton wrote. It's becoming an expensive habit for Raspberry Pi customers. The 16GB Pi 5 cost $120 when it launched in January 2025, which seems almost reasonable now. Raspberry Pi added $25 in December, another $60 in February, and a further $100 in April . With today's $80 increase, buyers are being asked to cough up $265 more than they were less than two years ago, a price hike of 221 percent. And it's barely been a month since Raspberry Pi raised prices on its 2GB Pi 4 and Pi 5 models by $12.50 apiece, taking them to $67.50 and $77.50 respectively. The repeated markups come despite Raspberry Pi reporting record first-half results in September. Revenue jumped 90 percent to $256.9 million, while gross profit rose 79 percent to $59.4 million. Gross profit per board climbed 53 percent to $12.20, helped partly by memory purchased before prices went through the roof. That stockpile advantage has since largely disappeared. For customers unwilling to pay nearly $400 for a single-board computer, Upton advises buying something with less RAM, using an older Pi, or optimizing applications to make do with less memory. He also warned that some sellers are exploiting the shortages by charging inflated prices or offering products that aren't what they appear to be, urging customers to stick to approved resellers. “We’re aware that a few bad actors have been taking advantage of the current memory supply circumstances to sell Raspberry Pi products at inflated prices or shift products that aren’t what they seem,” he said. There is, apparently, some good news, as Raspberry Pi continues to insist the increases are temporary. "As we've said from the beginning, the current memory landscape is difficult but ultimately temporary, and we look forward to rolling back our price increases when memory costs fall once again," Upton wrote. That could be a long wait. Micron has previously warned that memory shortages could drag on into 2028 or beyond, so anyone hoping to see a $120 Pi 5 again probably shouldn't hold their breath. ®

item.title: Dave Portnoy names the NFL team with ‘no apparent weakness’
item.description: Photo by Erica Denhoff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Dave Portnoy has had high praise for the Chicago Bears on the back of their latest win. The Bears were in Monday Night Football action against the Seattle Seahawks, who have struggled this term on the back of a dominant 2025/26. When all was said and done, Chicago came away with a 34-17 win, which included Caleb Williams securing 247 passing yards and one touchdown. Now, Portnoy has come out to suggest the Bears are favourites for the NFC and said that they have ‘no apparent weaknesses’. Dave Portnoy says the Chicago Bears have ‘no apparent weakness’ Taking to X/Twitter, he wrote: “I’m about to fall asleep, but before I do, I am declaring this Bears win the most impressive win of the season. “They got to be the favourite in the NFC. No apparent weaknesses.” After beating the Seahawks, the Bears are now 6-2 for the season, leaving them second in the NFC North behind the Minnesota Vikings who recently saw their unbeaten run come to an end against the Detroit Lions. The Bears are now due to return to the field this weekend when they play host to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers who are 3-5 after Week 8, in which they beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0. item.title: McNamara to succeed Cullen as Leinster head coach
item.description: Noel McNamara will remain with Bordeaux until the end of the season before he returns to Leinster [Getty Images] Noel McNamara will replace Leo Cullen as Leinster's head coach from next season, the Irish province have announced. Cullen said in June that he would leave his role at the end of the current campaign after a trophy-laden 12 years with Leinster. McNamara is currently attack coach at Bordeaux Begles, who defeated Leinster in the Investec Champions Cup final last season. The 43-year-old previously spent five years at Leinster in a number of roles, including Leinster 'A' head coach and as academy manager He joined the Sharks in South Africa in 2021 as attack and backs coach before he took on his current role with Bordeaux in 2023. Since moving to France, he has helped UBB win consecutive Champions Cups and they have twice been runners-up in the Top 14. In May, Leinster were second best as they struggled to deal with Bordeaux's McNamara-led attack in Bilbao as the French side ran out dominant 41-19 winners. McNamara, who also coached Ireland to an Under-20s Six Nations Grand Slam in 2019, said that the job was "one of the most prestigious roles in world rugby". "It is an honour to be given this responsibility," he said. "We have a very exciting season ahead with UBB and I am fully focused on that before moving back to Leinster next summer." Shane Nolan, Leinster's chief executive, said that McNamara was the province's "preferred candidate". "Noel has a long association with the club and emerged as our preferred candidate very early in the process," he said. "His transition into the role will be seamless and we look forward to welcoming him here next July after this season reaches its conclusion." The IRFU's performance director David Humhpreys said that McNarama has a "deep understanding of Irish rugby". "Noel brings a wealth of coaching experience, strong leadership qualities and a proven track record of developing players and coaching successful teams," he said. "I'm looking forward to working with him to ensure Leinster's continued success, while supporting the development of players for the Ireland national team." Since he took over in 2015, Cullen has led Leinster to six league titles and the Champions Cup in 2018, but his side subsequently lost five finals in the competition, including four in the past five years. Cullen to leave Leinster at end of next season

item.title: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo! Hammers confirm coaching change after West Brom defeat as replacement confirmed
item.description: West Ham United v West Bromwich Albion - Sky Bet Championship 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport West Ham United have officially parted ways with head coach Nuno Espirito Santo as the club attempts to rescue its promotion ambitions. The former Wolves and Tottenham boss departs following a difficult start to life in the Championship after the Hammers were relegated from the top flight last term. A faltering start in the Championship The east London outfit decided to retain Nuno despite suffering Premier League relegation last season, hoping for an immediate return to the top flight. However, consecutive league defeats have forced the board's hand, with his dismissal triggered by a dismal 3-1 home loss to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday. Frustrations boiled over at the London Stadium during the weekend defeat, with sections of the home support singing that the manager would be 'sacked in the morning'. After 13 league matches, the Hammers have managed just six victories and currently sit eighth in the table - occupying the final spot in the Championship's newly reconfigured play-off structure. Club statement confirms departure West Ham released a comprehensive official statement on Tuesday morning to confirm the coaching change. "West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect," the club announced. "Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track." The backroom staff will also see a major overhaul. The statement continued: "Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed. West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future." Club statement. Read more: https://t.co/LT0TZXbSpR pic.twitter.com/0r6Yz55iRi — West Ham United (@WestHam) November 3, 2026 Following the weekend loss that sealed his fate, Nuno was directly asked about the mounting scrutiny surrounding his position. "I am always under pressure," the manager admitted. "Every day." item.content:encoded: West Ham United v West Bromwich Albion - Sky Bet Championship 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport West Ham United have officially parted ways with head coach Nuno Espirito Santo as the club attempts to rescue its promotion ambitions. The former Wolves and Tottenham boss departs following a difficult start to life in the Championship after the Hammers were relegated from the top flight last term. A faltering start in the Championship The east London outfit decided to retain Nuno despite suffering Premier League relegation last season, hoping for an immediate return to the top flight. However, consecutive league defeats have forced the board's hand, with his dismissal triggered by a dismal 3-1 home loss to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday. Frustrations boiled over at the London Stadium during the weekend defeat, with sections of the home support singing that the manager would be 'sacked in the morning'. After 13 league matches, the Hammers have managed just six victories and currently sit eighth in the table - occupying the final spot in the Championship's newly reconfigured play-off structure. Club statement confirms departure West Ham released a comprehensive official statement on Tuesday morning to confirm the coaching change. "West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect," the club announced. "Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track." The backroom staff will also see a major overhaul. The statement continued: "Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed. West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future." Club statement. Read more: https://t.co/LT0TZXbSpR pic.twitter.com/0r6Yz55iRi — West Ham United (@WestHam) November 3, 2026 Following the weekend loss that sealed his fate, Nuno was directly asked about the mounting scrutiny surrounding his position. "I am always under pressure," the manager admitted. "Every day." Noble steps up amid managerial search With the hunt for a permanent successor already active, West Ham have turned to familiar faces to steady the ship. The statement detailed: "The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway." Club legend Mark Noble has been tasked with leading the squad in the short term alongside Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville. The club concluded: "Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of squad preparations ahead of tomorrow evening’s EFL Championship fixture at Cardiff City, and the Club will make no further comment until the appointment of the new Head Coach is confirmed." Crucial away days loom Noble and his interim coaching staff face a quick turnaround before Wednesday evening's trip to Wales to play Cardiff City. The Hammers desperately need to arrest their two-game losing streak and consolidate their fragile play-off position. Following the midweek clash, West Ham face another test on the road against Blackburn Rovers at Ewood Park on Saturday afternoon. A positive return from these two away fixtures is vital to keep the club's promotion aspirations alive while the boardroom finalises their next appointment.

item.title: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo
item.description: West Ham have sacked manager Nuno Espirito Santo following back-to-back defeats in the Championship. The Hammers’ promotion campaign has stalled following the home losses to Southampton and West Brom at the London Stadium, with the club sitting 8th after 13 games. Nuno, who oversaw West Ham’s relegation from the Premier League last season , had been expected to deliver an instant return to the top-flight . A club statement said: “West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect. “Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.” Former West Ham captain Mark Noble, along with Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville, will take temporary charge for Wednesday night’s trip to Cardiff. The club added that the search for a new head coach is underway, with Nuno’s assistant, Rui Pedro Silva, and goalkeeper coach, Rui Barbosa, also departing. “West Ham would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the club, and wish them all the very best for the future,” the club said. Nuno, the former Wolves, Tottenham and Nottingham Forest boss, replaced Graham Potter at the London Stadium in September 2025 and had signed a three-year contract. But the club’s 13-year stay in the top-flight came to an end as they finished 18th and were relegated to the Championship on the final day of the season, with Tottenham staying up instead . West Ham retained the services of captain Jarrod Bowen to boost their promotion bid, while the club also made the Championship record signing of Arne Engels from Celtic for £22m. The Hammers appeared to be on track for a Premier League return when they thrashed Wrexham 6-0 at the start of September, but that has been followed by just two wins in seven games. Fans turned on Nuno following the 2-1 defeat to West Brom on Saturday, as many of the 61,125-capacity crowd turned for the exits before full-time. West Ham fell to back-to-back defeats against West Brom (Getty) More follows

item.title: Oak Ridge opens winter sports league registration
item.description: The city of Oak Ridge Recreation & Parks Department has opened registration for its 2026-27 winter basketball leagues. Registration for the winter co-ed volleyball league begins Nov. 9. Basketball registration will close Nov. 14. Co-ed volleyball registration will run from Nov. 9 through Dec. 12, according to a city news release. The teen basketball league will be held Saturday mornings and is open to anyone 18 or younger who has not played TSSAA basketball during the 2026-27 school year and is currently enrolled in school. Boys and girls basketball divisions will be offered. Basketball games are scheduled to begin Dec. 10. Co-ed volleyball matches are scheduled to begin Jan. 5 and will be held Tuesday evenings. Interested teams may obtain registration information at the front desk of the Oak Ridge Civic Center or by emailing Matt Reece at mreece@oakridgetn.gov . For more information, call the Recreation Center at 865-425-3450. This article originally appeared on Oakridger: Oak Ridge opens winter sports league registration

item.title: Boy arrested following Bradley Lowery taunt
item.description: Black Cats fan Bradley died at the age of six in 2017 [Press Association] A 14-year-old boy has been arrested on suspicion of a public order offence and subsequently bailed, after a video on social media appeared to show a Coventry City fan taunting opposition Sunderland fans with a photo of Bradley Lowery. Sunderland fan Bradley, who died aged six in 2017 after being diagnosed with a rare childhood cancer, captured the hearts of the football world. The 14-year-old handed himself into West Midlands Police, who said they were investigating the incident. The Sky Blues added they were also investigating the footage from Saturday's Premier League match and Bradley's mother, Gemma, issued an emotional statement. "So much of Bradley's short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face," she posted on Instagram. "To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt." Her "beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate," Lowery said in an update through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, which raises funds and awareness to help and support children with cancer. She added she did not want hatred directing at the teenager involved, but instead wanted him to learn from his actions. A spokesperson for the club said: "Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland [on Saturday]." "The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action." West Midlands Police added they understood the upset the video had caused and were keeping Bradley's family updated as the investigation continued. Follow BBC Coventry & Warwickshire on BBC Sounds , Facebook , X and Instagram . item.title: Farinas, Gordon start in a 4-2-3-1: How Barcelona can line up against Aston Villa
item.description: Farinas, Gordon start in a 4-2-3-1: How Barcelona can line up against Aston Villa Barcelona return to Champions League action against Aston Villa at the Spotify Camp Nou on Tuesday, November 3, looking to recover from their defeat to Paris Saint-Germain and strengthen their position in the league phase standings. Hansi Flick’s side currently sit eighth with six points, three behind Unai Emery’s visitors, making victory particularly important as the competition progresses. Unfortunately, Barcelona’s defensive record under Flick has been quite concerning, with the team conceding in each of their last 18 Champions League fixtures. With several first-team defenders unavailable and the fixture schedule offering little opportunity for recovery, Flick will have to carefully manage his selection. On that note, changes are expected in defence, while the midfield and attacking departments offer continuity ahead of a demanding encounter against Aston Villa. Defence Gerard Martin could return to the starting XI against Astov Villa. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Joan Garcia is expected to continue in goal, with Flick having little reason to make a change between the posts. The bigger selection questions concern the defensive positions, where injuries to Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart have significantly reduced the manager’s options. One possibility is to use Brian Farinas at right-back and Joao Cancelo on the opposite flank, with Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin occupying the central defensive positions. Martin’s inclusion would be an important opportunity for the youngster, who featured as a second-half substitute against Alaves last weekend. De Jong was deployed at centre-back during that match, but with the Dutchman ready to return to his preferred midfield position, Flick could restore Martin to the starting defensive unit. Midfield Barcelona will count on Fermin Lopez’s return. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Barcelona’s midfield selection appears considerably more straightforward. Fermin Lopez should retain his place after producing an outstanding performance against Alaves, scoring once and providing two assists. Dani Olmo’s absence further strengthens Fermín’s chances of starting. His ability to arrive inside the penalty area and contribute directly makes him particularly important in a fixture where Barcelona will need to create opportunities against an organised Aston Villa defence. Pedri and Rodri are also expected to feature, giving Flick a combination of technical quality, creativity and control in central areas. Pedri’s workload will be worth monitoring, however, after he was substituted at half-time in the previous league fixture. Flick has alternatives available, including Gavi and Marc Bernal, but changing the midfield combination after such an encouraging performance against Alaves would be difficult to justify. Attack Anthony Gordon could join Raphinha and Lamine Yamal in the attack. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) The most interesting attacking selection decision concerns the left wing. Anthony Gordon is expected to have an opportunity to return to the starting XI after coming off the bench against Alaves, potentially joining Raphinha and Lamine Yamal in the forward line. Yamal arrives after scoring twice against Alaves, providing another reminder of his importance to Barcelona’s attacking plans. Raphinha’s intensity and movement should complement the teenager’s creativity, while Gordon would offer pace and direct running from the left. Karim Adeyemi could consequently drop to the bench following his substitution against Alaves.

item.title: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo after poor start to Championship season
item.description: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo after poor start to Championship season West Ham have sacked Nuno Espirito Santo with immediate effect, with the club eighth in the Championship and short of the automatic promotion places. Nuno's final game was Saturday's 3-1 home defeat by West Bromwich Albion, a result that saw the visitors move above West Ham in the table. It followed a 3-2 home loss to Southampton on October 24. Promotion push stalls West Ham were widely expected to bounce straight back to the Premier League after last season's relegation, and Nuno was tasked with leading that return. Instead, the East London club have won only six of their 13 league games, drawing four and losing three. That haul leaves them six points behind leaders Middlesbrough and four adrift of second-placed Swansea City. The Portuguese coach, 52, is not leaving alone. West Ham have confirmed that assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also left the club. "West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect," the club statement said. "Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track. "Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed. "West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future." A reprieve that did not last Nuno arrived on a three-year contract in September 2025, replacing the sacked Graham Potter with West Ham 19th in the Premier League . He was unable to keep them up, and relegation was confirmed on the final day of the season. His position had already come under scrutiny within months of his appointment, but the club opted to keep faith with him in January. Days after relegation was sealed, West Ham issued a statement confirming he would stay on. Before West Ham, Nuno managed Wolverhampton Wanderers, Tottenham Hotspur and Nottingham Forest. Club legend Mark Noble will take temporary charge alongside Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville, with West Ham travelling to Cardiff City on Wednesday night.

item.title: For the Girls, For Our Health: The Active Circle x Zephans & Co. Celebrate Breast Cancer Awareness Month With The Girls’ Club
item.description: Breast Cancer Awareness Month ended on the most vibrant, empowering note in Lagos! The Active Circle , powered by contemporary fashion brand Zephans & Co. , brought together fabulous women from all walks of life for The Girls’ Club – a dreamy, pink-hued wellness wonderland created to celebrate womanhood while championing critical conversations around breast health. The morning kicked off on a high-energy note with a beginner-friendly Pilates session led by top instructor Dammy Olufowobi , proving that movement can be both joyful and deeply rewarding. Adhering to the chic Pretty in Pink dress code, attendees transformed the studio into an editorial runway of blush and beauty. Beyond the movement and aesthetic moments, the heart of the event was an intimate “Breast Talk” session delivered by Dr. Omolola Salako – widely known as The People’s Oncologist . Dr. Salako unpacked the importance of early detection, self-examinations, and practical steps for proactive health, making the conversation feel personal, approachable, and empowering. Chisom Okuguni, Convener of The Active Circle, shared that the initiative was designed to equip women with the knowledge and community support needed to prioritize their well-being every single day. The wellness morning provided an opportunity for the ladies to interact and share experiences, connect on a deeper level, all while learning to care for their breast health. Proudly supported by BellaNaija , The Girls’ Club proved that when women come together for movement, health, and community, magic happens. BellaNaija is a Media Partner for The Girls Club The post For the Girls, For Our Health: The Active Circle x Zephans & Co. Celebrate Breast Cancer Awareness Month With The Girls’ Club appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: "Antonio was the bigger talent" – Norwegian coach reflects on working with Nusa and Haaland ahead of RB Leipzig vs Man City clash
item.description: "Antonio was the bigger talent" – Norwegian coach reflects on working with Nusa and Haaland ahead of RB Leipzig vs Man City clash Two Norwegian stars go head-to-head on Wednesday night as Antonio Nusa and RB Leipzig welcome Erling Haaland and Manchester City to the Red Bull Arena in the Champions League. Having coached Haaland at Bryne FK and Nusa at Stabæk Fotball, Gaute Larsen knows both players well and has shared some fascinating insights into their formative years ahead of Wednesday’s clash. “I’ve been a professional coach for 35 years, and [Nusa] was one of the most technically gifted and talented players I’ve ever seen,” Larsen, who first watched Nusa play when the Norwegian winger was just 13 or 14, told RB Leipzig’s club media. “Antonio was exceptional on the ball. He had great balance, was a fantastic dribbler and knew when to pass and when to take someone on,” added the 64-year-old. Haaland, meanwhile, had some challenges to overcome on his journey to becoming one of the world’s best strikers. “Erling was very tall and skinny, and he moved a bit like Bambi on ice. At 14 or 15, he didn’t have the same balance or ball control that Antonio had at that age," Larsen explained, admitting that he rated Nusa more highly when comparing the two at the same stage of their development. “When they were both young, Antonio was the bigger talent in my eyes," he stressed. Now in his third season at RB Leipzig, Nusa has taken his attacking output to another level, racking up five goals and seven assists in 13 appearances so far this campaign. “I think we’re only just starting to see the best of Antonio. As he grows in confidence, he’s going to get even better," Larsen said. The coach also praised Nusa’s character, stressing that his qualities extend well beyond the pitch. “Antonio is very down-to-earth, both as a player and as a person. He looks after his friends and family. He’s a role model for young players," he said. Nusa has had at least one goal involvement in each of his last three outings and will be hoping to extend that run against Haaland and Manchester City on Wednesday at 21:00 CEST.

item.title: Five Champions League talking points: Carrick's Roma memories, Villa face Barcelona test
item.description: Five Champions League talking points: Carrick's Roma memories, Villa face Barcelona test The Champions League returns this week with plenty of intriguing storylines, from Manchester United 's reunion with a famous European opponent to Aston Villa 's latest test against one of the continent's elite. Paris Saint-Germain are looking to continue their remarkable dominance of the competition, while Liverpool head to Istanbul for a reunion with a familiar face. Elsewhere, a former Real Madrid flop will be hoping to make his old employers regret letting him go. Here are five talking points ahead of this week's Champions League action. Can Carrick draw inspiration from Manchester United's famous Roma night? Michael Carrick 's status as Manchester United manager appears to be on life support right now, with a nine-game winless run in all competitions seeing some suggest the axe is being sharpened. Off-field tensions and a string of disappointing performances have intensified scrutiny, ahead of Tuesday's Champions League meeting with AS Roma at Old Trafford. The clash with Roma will evoke memories of one of Carrick's finest nights. The midfielder scored twice as Manchester United thrashed the Serie A side 7-1 in the 2006/07 quarter-finals, as Sir Alex Ferguson's side bounced back from poor recent results to deliver one of the most memorable European nights in club history. How Carrick could do with a repeat. Barcelona provide biggest test yet of Aston Villa's European progress Aston Villa's farcical fallout with Jamie Carragher this week was an unneeded distraction to what has been a quietly impressive start to the season. Despite mass exits in the summer, Villa are unbeaten in their last five Premier League games, and have maximum points in the Champions League. Villa are determined to establish themselves among the elite of English and European football, and their performances in the Champions League offer plenty of encouragement. Unai Emery's side became the second quickest team in European Cup/Champions League history to record 20 wins in the competition last time out, achieving the feat in only their 30th fixture. Only Real Madrid (29 games) have reached that milestone quicker. Villa face a huge test of their progress this week, with a trip to face Barcelona at Camp Nou. Will anyone stop a Paris Saint-Germain three-peat? Having conquered Europe in each of the previous two seasons, Paris Saint-Germain have started the new campaign in ominous fashion. Luis Enrique's men lead the league phase table with a perfect record after three games, ahead of this week's meeting with Villarreal. PSG have achieved maximum points in style. The back-to-back Champions League winners have set a new record for goals scored after three Champions League group games (14), despite facing sides considered contenders in Manchester City and Barcelona. The French side are formidable. Dirk Kuyt reunion adds intrigue to Liverpool's Istanbul trip Liverpool also have a perfect record

The French side are formidable. Dirk Kuyt reunion adds intrigue to Liverpool's Istanbul trip Liverpool also have a perfect record after three games ahead of a visit to Istanbul this week. The Reds takes on Fenerbahce at The Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium, with the usual ferocious atmosphere expected. The fixture takes on an intriguing sub-plot, after the appointment of ex-Liverpool favourite Dirk Kuyt as interim manager of the Turkish side. Kuyt scored 71 goals in 285 games across six seasons at Anfield, including a consolation in the 2007 Champions League final. Now tasked with reviving Fenerbahce's faltering season, Kuyt has an immediate opportunity to make an impression against his former club. Luka Jovic has a point to prove against former club Real Madrid Luka Jovic's Real Madrid career never came close to matching expectations. Signed for €60m after an outstanding spell at Eintracht Frankfurt, the Serbian striker managed just three goals in 51 appearances for the Spanish giants. After a poor period post-Madrid, Jovic has found a home at AEK Athens. The 28-year-old has scored 28 goals in 58 games for the club and fired AEK to Greek Super League success last season. He comes face-to-face with his old side in the Greek capital this week, and will want to prove a point.

item.title: Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision
item.description: Forward had cardiac arrest and was taken to hospital He was struck in the chest when challenging for ball The Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel has died as a result of injuries sustained in a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono in their second division match. “From CD Tenerife, we announce the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00am, of Jesús de Miguel Alameda,” the club said in a statement. “No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news.” Continue reading...

item.title: Slow start 'toughest' time of Eustace managerial career
item.description: [BBC] Derby County boss John Eustace says the opening three months of the season have been the "toughest" of his managerial career. The Rams are in the relegation places with just one win from 13 Championship games so far this term. The slow start to the season follows a drawn-out and ultimately failed takeover attempt at the club during the summer, compounded by injury woes which have forced a number of key players out of action. Former Blackburn Rovers and Birmingham City boss Eustace, who has come under increasing pressure to keep his job in recent weeks, admits the Rams side he guided to within four points of the play-off places last term are now in a fight to avoid the drop. "It's been the toughest three months, definitely, through recruitment and personnel that are available to us," he told BBC East Midlands Today. "But it's part of the job and I have to get my head around that and try to find solutions." Derby, whose defeat by Millwall on Saturday was their sixth loss in a nine-match winless run, host Norwich City on Tuesday night. Latest Derby County news, analysis and fan views

item.title: Dave Portnoy hammers LeBron James for setting wrong example for kids after mid-game sip of wine
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images LeBron James’ viral moment with a Philadelphia 76ers fan has upset Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy. LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers are unstoppable at the moment as they have extended their winning streak to four games and hold a league-best 7-1 record at the moment. The 76ers’ most recent win came against the Chicago Bulls as the host utterly dominated the visitors in a 126-107 result. While it was a terrific result, the thing that has caught the eye of Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy was James’ viral moment with a 76ers fan. Dave Portnoy calls out LeBron James for sipping wine mid-game The 41-year-old forward went viral for his courtside interaction with a fan after crashing into him. Instead of directly returning to the court, James took a sip from the fan’s glass of wine. While most found this hilarious, Portnoy was furious with James and claimed that the 76ers star is setting a bad example for his younger fans. “If anybody else did this, they’d be checked into AA, but because it’s Bron-Bron, SportCenter will do an hour special on it. Who cares [about] the example it sets for kids that you need to be drunk to play sports?” Portnoy stated on X . For what it’s worth, NBA fans didn’t like Portnoy’s comments and called him out for unnecessarily hating on the King. But will that stop Portnoy from taking jabs at James? Most likely not. After all, Portnoy has always been very vocal about his stance against the 4x NBA champion. item.description: Jon Rahm reveals the changes to LIV 2.0 that made him quit the tour, whilst also admitting that he'd take the same deal as Brooks Koepka to re-join the PGA Tour if the offer was still on the table.

item.title: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo after poor start to season
item.description: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo after poor start to season West Ham sack Nuno Espírito Santo as Championship promotion bid falters West Ham have dismissed Nuno Espírito Santo after a disappointing start to their Championship campaign, with the club turning to an interim coaching team before Wednesday’s visit to Cardiff City. The decision follows a 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion that left West Ham eighth in the table. According to ESPN, they are four points outside the automatic promotion places after relegation from the Premier League last season. Nuno had remained in charge with the responsibility of securing an immediate return to the top flight. That task will now pass to a successor, while Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville take temporary control of the team. Photo IMAGO Nuno departure follows West Brom defeat The weekend loss proved to be Nuno’s final match in charge, bringing an end to a spell that included West Ham’s relegation. Remaining with the manager had offered continuity as the club attempted to rebuild in the Championship. The expectation was that he would guide them back towards the Premier League, but their opening results have left them outside even the play-off positions. Eighth place does not put promotion beyond reach. The four-point gap to the top two shows that the leading positions remain relatively close. Nevertheless, West Ham have decided that their progress under Nuno has not been sufficient to continue with the same leadership. The dismissal changes the direction of their season before the automatic promotion places have moved too far away, but it also creates an immediate need for stability around the squad. Noble and coaching colleagues take temporary charge Noble, Potts and Prenderville will oversee preparations for the trip to Cardiff, giving the club an interim arrangement while the managerial position remains unresolved. Their first assignment comes quickly. Wednesday’s away match offers little time to make extensive changes, placing the emphasis on preparing the existing players for the next fixture. The temporary appointments should not be confused with the announcement of a permanent successor. ESPN’s report does not name a replacement for Nuno or provide a timetable for that decision. For now, the responsibility is to help West Ham respond to the defeat against West Brom and prevent the disruption from affecting another result. A managerial change can alter the mood around a team, but the immediate demands remain practical: organise preparations, clarify responsibilities and produce a better performance. Coaching departures extend beyond head coach Nuno is not the only member of the staff leaving. Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also departed, meaning West Ham’s change involves several figures responsible for preparing the team. The temporary appointments should not be confused with the announcement of a permanent successor. ESPN’s report does not name a replacement for Nuno or provide a timetable for that decision. For now, the responsibility is to help West Ham respond to the defeat against West Brom and prevent the disruption from affecting another result. A managerial change can alter the mood around a team, but the immediate demands remain practical: organise preparations, clarify responsibilities and produce a better performance. Coaching departures extend beyond head coach Nuno is not the only member of the staff leaving. Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also departed, meaning West Ham’s change involves several figures responsible for preparing the team. That makes the interim coaching arrangements particularly important. Players must adjust to different voices while maintaining their focus on a promotion campaign that remains competitive. The next permanent appointment will also need to establish how the coaching operation should function. The report offers no details of potential candidates or the approach West Ham intend to take in their search. Until those decisions are announced, Noble, Potts and Prenderville provide the immediate leadership. Promotion remains central to West Ham’s next decision The broader objective has not changed with Nuno’s departure. West Ham are seeking a return to the Premier League after last season’s relegation, and their next appointment will be judged against that ambition. The current table creates both pressure and opportunity. Being eighth falls short of an automatic promotion position, but a four-point deficit leaves scope to recover ground. That balance will shape the task facing the next manager. There is a campaign to improve, rather than a promotion challenge already beyond repair. For West Ham, the Cardiff fixture is the first test of their response. Nuno’s exit closes one chapter, but the outcome of the decision will depend on whether the team can turn a change of leadership into more convincing results.

item.title: David Adelman ‘Embarrassed’ After Nuggets Loss to Trail Blazers
item.description: David Adelman Nuggets Getty Denver Nuggets head coach David Adelman said he was “embarrassed” after Denver lost at home to the Portland Trail Blazers. The Nuggets lost 118-110 at home at Ball Arena on Monday night to the Trail Blazers, dropping Denver’s record this season to 3-3. Afterwards, coach Adelman said he was “embarrassed” by the team’s effort in the game, particularly on the glass, as Portland outrebounded Denver 53 to 37. David Adelman Unhappy With Nuggets in Loss to Trail Blazers Speaking to reporters after the game, Adelman couldn’t help but reveal his frustration with his team’s compete level against Portland. “Adelman was ’embarrassed’ by DEN’s effort in the 50/50 rebs tonight. He acknowledged Clingan’s 9 OREB, but pointed out that they had lots of smaller guys crashing too, and the other half occurred because of those mistakes. Ultimately, DEN got their ‘ass kicked’ in that category,” per Nuggets reporter Brendan Vogt . Adelman was “embarrassed” by DEN’s effort in the 50/50 rebs tonight. He acknowledged Clingan’s 9 OREB, but pointed out that they had lots of smaller guys crashing too, and the other half occurred because of those mistakes. Ultimately, DEN got their “ass kicked” in that category — Brendan Vogt (@BrendanVogt) November 3, 2026 David Adelman’s Job Could Be in Jeopardy Given Denver’s mediocre start to the season, the calls for Adelman to lose his job are coming in from Nuggets fans, who are getting tired of seeing their team look sluggish and unprepared, especially at home, where they are just 1-2 this season. The Nuggets have one of the most expensive rosters in the NBA , so there is no way that the team’s ownership group is happy about the product that the team is putting out on the floor at the moment, as Denver’s performances have just been unacceptable for a veteran-laden squad with as many highly paid players as they have on the roster. While it is still obviously very early in the season, Nuggets fans have questioned Adelman’s hiring ever since he was promoted to head coach following the team’s late-season firing of former head coach Mike Malone two years ago. Anytime you have Nikola Jokic on your roster, anything less than an NBA Championship is seen as a disappointment. For many Nuggets fans out there, until the team goes and makes the decision to fire Adelman and bring in someone else to lead the team, they’re going to feel that their team isn’t going to win this year. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post David Adelman ‘Embarrassed’ After Nuggets Loss to Trail Blazers appeared first on HEAVY .

Ultimately, DEN got their “ass kicked” in that category — Brendan Vogt (@BrendanVogt) November 3, 2026 David Adelman’s Job Could Be in Jeopardy Given Denver’s mediocre start to the season, the calls for Adelman to lose his job are coming in from Nuggets fans, who are getting tired of seeing their team look sluggish and unprepared, especially at home, where they are just 1-2 this season. The Nuggets have one of the most expensive rosters in the NBA , so there is no way that the team’s ownership group is happy about the product that the team is putting out on the floor at the moment, as Denver’s performances have just been unacceptable for a veteran-laden squad with as many highly paid players as they have on the roster. While it is still obviously very early in the season, Nuggets fans have questioned Adelman’s hiring ever since he was promoted to head coach following the team’s late-season firing of former head coach Mike Malone two years ago. Anytime you have Nikola Jokic on your roster, anything less than an NBA Championship is seen as a disappointment. For many Nuggets fans out there, until the team goes and makes the decision to fire Adelman and bring in someone else to lead the team, they’re going to feel that their team isn’t going to win this year. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post David Adelman ‘Embarrassed’ After Nuggets Loss to Trail Blazers appeared first on HEAVY .

item.content:encoded: Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers lays the ball up during an NBA basketball game against the Miami Heat, Monday November 2, 2026 in Los Angeles, Calif. LOS ANGELES — There is a specific kind of tired that comes from a back-to-back — the kind that sits in your calves, fogs the back of your eyes and makes the rim look a quarter-inch smaller than it did yesterday. Most teams bring that tired with them onto the court like luggage. They drag it up the floor. They let it seep into the jump shots and the closeouts and the late rotations. The Lakers left theirs at the door. On Monday night at Crypto.com Arena, on the second night of a back-to-back, against a Miami Heat team starring Giannis Antetokounmpo in his debut season in South Beach, the Lakers played their best game of the young season — a 138-117 thrashing so complete, so rhythmic, so casually dominant that it felt less like a basketball game and more like a campaign rally with a scoreboard. 57 percent shooting. 19 made threes. A season-high 39 assists. 41 bench points. And at the center of it all, the man who is making the MVP conversation feel less like a debate and more like a formality. Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 42 points, 13 assists, seven rebounds and two steals. His fourth 40-point game in his last five. His fifth consecutive game scoring at least 37. And somewhere in the third quarter, between a step-back three that broke Miami's spirit and a skip pass that broke its defense, the basketball world quietly crossed a threshold. Start with the numbers, because they're the whole argument. Over his last five games, Dončić is averaging 43.4 points, 8.4 rebounds, and 8.6 assists with 2.0 steals, shooting 53.2% from the field, 44.7% from three, and 89.1% from the free-throw line. That's not a hot streak; that's a residency. Dončić has been in this zone so long he's paying property taxes on it. Nightly, he continues to etch out his name in Laker lore. Dončić has tied Jerry West for the 14th-most 40-point games. He has 66 of them. He is only 27 years old. Let that sit. 66 career 40-point games — equal to the Logo himself. 22 of them as a Laker, sixth in franchise history, a list that includes Elgin Baylor, West, Kobe Bryant, Shaquille O'Neal and the man whose name is on the building's soul. And with Monday's performance — his 29th career 40-point, 10-assist game, third-most in NBA history — Dončić passed James Harden for the most games ever with 40+ points, 10+ assists and 5+ made threes. Harden's record didn't survive the calendar turning November. Dončić is methodical with how he engages defenses. He knows what to avoid and how to execute his plan. His cadence is deliberate and pensive. Not rushed. Measured. It's slow, yet effective. Dončić plays in between the notes. His lethality is equally uncanny and unorthodox. Ziaire Williams, watching from the other end of the floor, put it more bluntly. "It's crazy, man. The defensive mindset in me is always like, why are they not blitzing him or why are they not doubling? Why are they just letting him walk to his spot and do whatever he wants out there? But they're trying. He just is that good and he just makes it look that easy," Williams said. They did blitz him. Miami threw doubles at him almost every possession, and it didn't matter, because Dončić has turned being trapped into a team asset. The ball left his hands, found the open man, and the open man — Sandro Mamukelashvili, Quentin Grimes, Williams — buried shots. 19 threes from seven different players. Five Lakers with multiple makes. "They obviously put two on me, so we just share the ball," Dončić said. "I mean, it's 39 assists, which is not bad." Not bad. 42 points and 13 assists, and the man's review of his own masterpiece is "not bad." The confidence isn't arrogance anymore; it's arithmetic. MVP campaigns aren't won alone, and Monday night made the case that this Lakers team might be the best version of itself yet — precisely because it doesn't need Dončić to do everything. Austin Reaves poured in 27 points on 10-of-15 shooting, 4-of-5 from deep, with five assists, attacking closeouts with the patience of a man who has made a career out of being underestimated. Walker Kessler went for 15 points and 15 rebounds — his 60th career double-double, his third straight. Throughout the night, Kessler blocked shots, erased mistakes and did the invisible work that turns a good defense into a wall. "He's a big key for us," Dončić said. "When he plays good it gives us a way better chance to win. Obviously he's not going to play every game great, but what he's been doing, it's helping us win a lot." And here's the number that should unsettle the rest of the league: the Lakers are plus-113 in Dončić's minutes this season. 113 points better with him on the floor. Through eight games. That's not a stat. That's nuts. The defense, once the question mark draped over this entire experiment, has become a talking point in its own right. JJ Redick challenged his team at halftime after Miami carved up the Lakers' transition defense for 40 points in the first eight seconds of possessions. The response: Miami managed just 16 fast-break points after the break and shot a paltry percentage in half-court-initiated offense. Redick called the second-half response "awesome." "We really challenged the guys at halftime," Redick said. "The biggest thing on the scout report was get back and get set. We gave up 40 in the first half. In the second half they were 7-for-... it was as good as you can hope for." The Lakers outscored Miami 60-38 in the paint, funneling Antetokounmpo—30 points, 12 rebounds and seven assists of honest, punishing effort—into a wall of bodies and a waiting Kessler. "You're not ever going to stop a guy like that," Reaves said. "We just hope to make it tough for him." Context matters in campaigns, and Monday's win came loaded with it. The Lakers played Friday, escaped Toronto on Sunday night, then faced a rested Heat team that hadn't played since Friday. Fatigue was the script. Fatigue got rewritten. "On paper, to play Toronto and then Miami back-to-back is not the easiest," Williams said. "But there's no excuses. Everyone's banged up, bruised up, but we got to figure it out." That's 6-2. That's consecutive comfortable wins on consecutive nights against two playoff-caliber opponents. That's a team that lost an ugly one to Golden State less than a week ago — a game where the blitzes and traps broke their offense into pieces — and has turned that weakness into a weapon every game since. It's almost as if whatever Golden State exposed, the Lakers fixed. And they fixed it fast, in real time, because the NBA schedule doesn't leave room for lengthy repairs. Redick, whose 39-assist total was the most since he's been head coach, summed up the state of the operation. "It's a really good offense that we're playing right now. And a lot of that is Dončić and what he's able to do to bend the defense," Redick said. There has never been a version of Dončić this complete; not in Dallas, not as a Laker. The points were always there. The genius was always there. What's new––what's campaign-defining––is everything else. The charges taken, two of them in the first quarter alone. The five steals. The feet moving on defense force ink on scouting reports, confirming that it is No. 77. It becomes contagious when your offensive superstar and leader takes two of his three charges in the first quarter. The answer was on the floor for 48 minutes. This is a team that figured out who it is faster than anyone predicted: a team with a top-four three-point shooting percentage, a rim-protecting center, a secondary creator in Reaves, and a bench that contributed 41 points on a night the starters could afford to rest the fourth. The MVP race is long. Antetokounmpo is going to put up numbers. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander exists. Jokić is Jokić. The season has 74 games left to argue abou

item.title: F1 Insists Qatar and Abu Dhabi Races Go On, Max Verstappen Doubts Teams Will Split
item.description: Max Verstappen says he doesn't expect F1 teams to split like MotoGP about racing in the Middle East. (Source: MEGA) Formula 1 has told its 11 teams the 2026 season will still end in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, after Yamaha pulled out of this week's MotoGP race in Qatar. Max Verstappen doesn't see the paddock cracking over it. The message went out during the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend. F1 still plans to race at Lusail on November 29 and at Yas Marina on December 6. The four-time world champion thinks F1 won't follow MotoGP down that road. "I don't think a situation similar to what happened in MotoGP will happen," Verstappen said, according to Autoracing1 . He added a catch, though: his view depends on the safety guarantees F1 can give and on what happens in the coming weeks. Max Verstappen raises concerns over F1 racing in Qatar and Abu Dhabi amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East. "It mainly depends on what kind of guarantees they can give us and what happens over the coming weeks." "You can say now that you're happy to go there, but you… pic.twitter.com/G5y1Mof378 — Everything Formula (@evrythngformu1a) November 2, 2026 Yamaha and its satellite team Pramac will skip the Qatar round, and MotoGP has threatened contract and sporting penalties. Both series now belong to Liberty Media, so the timing stings. F1 says neither the travel advice nor the insurance situation has changed since May, and it's watching events closely, including the U.S. midterm elections. F1 Asks Teams and Drivers to Trust the Plan The message asks teams and drivers not to speak too critically in public, as F1 did earlier this year over the technical rules. Teams should trust F1 and the FIA and repeat the public line they've used for weeks. ESPN , which also saw the message, says it warns teams against getting dragged into media speculation. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies showed how that sounds. He said F1 and the FIA hold the full set of information, so Red Bull relies on them to make the right call, and he added that they've got most of these calls right in the past. Williams team principal James Vowles voiced similar views. Laurent Mekies, like Max Verstappen, says he trusts the governing body to do the right thing about the Middle East situation. (Source: MEGA) F1 backs the message with a Plan B. Organizers at Imola got the green light more than six weeks ago to build temporary grandstands, and F1 has agreed to cover the costs if the circuit isn't needed. The fallback date would be December 6, in Europe. F1 also says it has evacuation plans at every race and has walked the teams through what would happen if they had to leave Qatar or Abu Dhabi in a hurry. One team source told ESPN that freight is moving as normal. With so much money involved, Autosport wrote, nobody wants to blink first. F1 chief executive Stefano Domenicali set the tone in early October. He said everything was confirmed for Qatar and Abu Dhabi, and that 99% of the tickets in Abu Dhabi had sold. Max

He said F1 and the FIA hold the full set of information, so Red Bull relies on them to make the right call, and he added that they've got most of these calls right in the past. (Source: MEGA) F1 backs the message with a Plan B. Organizers at Imola got the green light more than six weeks ago to build temporary grandstands, and F1 has agreed to cover the costs if the circuit isn't needed. The fallback date would be December 6, in Europe. F1 also says it has evacuation plans at every race and has walked the teams through what would happen if they had to leave Qatar or Abu Dhabi in a hurry. One team source told ESPN that freight is moving as normal. With so much money involved, Autosport wrote, nobody wants to blink first. F1 chief executive Stefano Domenicali set the tone in early October. He said everything was confirmed for Qatar and Abu Dhabi, and that 99% of the tickets in Abu Dhabi had sold. Max Verstappen Walks a Careful Line on Qatar Max Verstappen has softened his stance since his comments before the Azerbaijan GP about racing in the Middle East. (Source: MEGA) Verstappen hasn't always sounded this measured. Before the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, he said that with a war nearby, "I think we shouldn't go," as he told Viaplay , though he added the decision wasn't his to make. GPblog reported at the time that his view put him at odds with seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton . In October, Verstappen softened his position. Asked if he might boycott, he said he loves going to the region under the right terms, and that he trusts F1 and the FIA because they have more information than drivers do. Mexico brought a lighter moment. When Dutch reporters raised the comments Carlos Sainz made in Austin, Verstappen laughed. "Someone will probably have had a word with him afterwards," he said. Someone was definitely not happy with what Carlos Sainz said yesterday Carlos Sainz in the press conference yesterday: "On my personal side and not speaking as GPDA, it's very difficult to be convinced right now that the races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will happen" Carlos Sainz 2… pic.twitter.com/pmUndLy9r7 — Pablo Martinez (Holiness) (@F1BigData) October 23, 2026 Sainz is the director of the Grand Prix Drivers' Association. Before the U.S. Grand Prix, the Williams driver said it was "very difficult to be convinced right now" that F1 should race in the Middle East, but he reversed course in a statement less than two hours later. That statement said he trusts F1 and the FIA to put safety first. Then Verstappen turned serious. "It also depends a bit on what they can guarantee in terms of safety," he said. He added that you can say today you're happy to go, but the region still isn't entirely stable. F1 wants one voice on this. Verstappen has given it one, but not without a footnote. The cars are due in Qatar in under four weeks.

item.title: “Couldn’t Be Prouder” – Alexander Zverev’s Girlfriend Sophia Thomalla Shares Emotional Message As German Receives World No. 1 Trophy In Paris
item.description: Sophia Thomalla (left) and Alexander Zverev (right), © Instagram/sophiathomalla) Alexander Zverev’s girlfriend Sophia Thomalla, the prominent German actress and model, shared an emotional message after Zverev received the World No. 1 trophy ahead of his Paris Masters campaign. According to Thomalla, Zverev is fully deserving of the top ranking in men’s singles tennis, which he secured just days ago by defeating Tallon Griekspoor in Vienna. It’s worth noting that Zverev had already secured the year-end No. 1 ranking prior to his win over Griekspoor. On Monday, Nov. 2, Zverev was presented the World No. 1 trophy by Andrea Gaudenzi, the ATP Chairman, and Cedric Pioline, the tournament director of the Paris Masters. Subsequently, Thomalla, who has been dating the German tennis star since late 2020, took to her Instagram and shared a carousel post celebrating her boyfriend’s latest high-profile achievement in the sport. She captioned the post: “Couldn’t be prouder of you. You deserve every bit of this. ❤️🏆 Nr.1!! Common!!” She also added separate captions to all of the subsequent pictures and videos in the post. Check Thomalla’s post out below: In terms of his tennis, Zverev suffered an upset in Vienna soon after securing his maiden ascent to the World No. 1 ranking. Alexander Zverev was beaten in the Vienna Open semifinals by Alex de Minaur In addition to helping him secure the No. 1 ranking, Zverev’s victory over Griekspoor in Vienna saw the German book a quarterfinal berth at the ATP 500 event. In the last eight, Zverev registered a dominant 6-0, 6-2 win over Arthur Fery of Great Britain. However, his Vienna campaign ended in the semifinals, with top 10 rival Alex de Minaur of Australia edging the German 6-4, 1-6, 7-6(4). The result once again led to scrutiny of Zverev’s No. 1 status, with many fans feeling that he has reached the summit of the rankings primarily because of rivals Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner’s injury issues. At the Paris Masters, Zverev is the top seed and has received a first-round bye. He is set to get his campaign at the year’s last Masters 1000 event underway with a tricky second-round match against former No. 5 Lorenzo Musetti of Italy. Musetti, currently ranked No. 24 and unseeded in Paris, defeated another former top 10 star, Hubert Hurkacz, in the first round. Concerningly for Zverev, the Italian leads their head-to-head 3-2 . item.title: A look at Evansville women's basketball entering Year 1 under Ben Wierzba
item.description: EVANSVILLE — Ben Wierzba has repeated the same word these last few weeks: resilient. That rings true in multiple ways as he begins first year with University of Evansville women's basketball. The Purple Aces face a program reset to begin the 2026-27 season. A new coach and near complete roster turnover following their best Missouri Valley Conference Tournament finish in nearly 20 years. UE also endured a challenging offseason that included the tragic passing of sophomore guard Jordan Scott in September . Hence why Wierzba sees a level of resiliency in his first team. "We’ve had a lot of situations that have happened in the last three months," he said. "This team has been able to lean upon each other, be there for each other. They come into work every day and give us everything they have. That’s all we can ask for." More: A look at Evansville men’s basketball entering Year 5 under David Ragland Here's a look at the team, which has already been hit by injuries, with the season starting Nov. 3 at DePaul. The Aces don't have a home game at Meeks Family Fieldhouse until Nov. 21 against Lindenwood. Laying the foundation in Year 1 under Ben Wierzba Wierzba understands the mindset is very cliché. He still believes the Aces will be exponentially better between now and March. It's probably true based on the current state of his lineup going into November. Evansville defeated IU East 64-45 on Oct. 25 in its lone exhibition contest. The Aces only had six available players. As of that date, it was only the team's sixth day of playing 5-on-5 since official practice commenced. That boils down to the simple fact that a decent chunk of the roster is injured. The ability to even field a lineup was notable. Remolding the program into a success won't happen overnight. Evansville hasn't produced a winning record since 2008 and or a finish over .500 in the Valley since 2014. The Aces went 10-25 last season under former coach Robyn Scherr and lost to Murray State in the MVC final. Only three players returned. "It doesn’t matter who we are playing," Wierzba said. "It’s always about us. Getting better each day and paying attention to our details. Everybody talks about how their team’s going to get better as the year goes along. I think our team is going to make exponential jumps because of being in 5-on-5 situations." The offseason was already a truncated process with Wierzba not being officially introduced as the head coach until April 24. He brought with him 25 years on the sideline as the Division I level, including 2007-10 with UE men's basketball on Marty Simmons' staff. Wierzba spent the last three as the associate head coach at Miami (Ohio) with the RedHawks making the NCAA Tournament last spring. UE started season prep while being limited on the court. The program had to recruit from other sports on campus to fill out the roster. That's on top of mourning the loss of a teammate and friend.
