He brought with him 25 years on the sideline as the Division I level, including 2007-10 with UE men's basketball on Marty Simmons' staff. Wierzba spent the last three as the associate head coach at Miami (Ohio) with the RedHawks making the NCAA Tournament last spring. UE started season prep while being limited on the court. The program had to recruit from other sports on campus to fill out the roster. That's on top of mourning the loss of a teammate and friend. Junior guard Avery Kelley pointed to Wierzba has the team's rock during an emotional offseason. "He’s the coach I’d want to have in my corner," she said. "The preseason was really tough for us. We went through a lot as a team and individually. He was the perfect coach for us. That coach that got us through this, pushed us through every day." Who will the Purple Aces count on in the 2026-27 season? The exhibition is tough to judge considering the roster's current limitations. It still provided an early look at who could play major minutes and how Weirzba would like the Aces to play. Evansville shot 49% with 20 assists on 23 made field goals. Turnovers were an issue with IU East's press causing the Aces to play too quickly. The bigger takeaway was the individuals assigned significant roles to start the season. Mireia Musfaros had 23 points and eight rebounds. Kelley, who missed most of last year with a knee injury, totaled 19 points, seven rebounds and six steals. Marina Artero added seven assists. Wierzba pointed to those three, along with junior guard Kaiden Kreinhagen, as the starting point for this season. He also likes the potential from his freshman class once they're healthy – only Kelyn Johnson was available against IU East. "We have girls that can shoot the lights out and have great posts," Kelley said. "On top of that, we have players with super high IQ. There’s a lot to look forward out of this team. I have teammates that can put the ball in the hoop. Teammates that will bust their butt on defense." More: 65 high school girls basketball players to watch in SW Indiana for 2026-27 season The exhibition was also the first look at sophomore Sophia Otten. The 6-foot-3 forward had seven points against IU East – a notable contribution considering she came to UE to play softball (18 appearances in the pitching circle last spring). Otten had Division II basketball offers coming out of Incarnate Word Academy in Missouri. Wierzba told Jevin Redman via the Aces on the Air podcast that additional athletes from the soccer program will join once the fall season is complete. The roster, let alone a working lineup, is very much a work in progress. "Avery, Kaiden and Mireia are the three returners," Wierzba said. "Great leaders for us. Then you’ve got Marina Artero that has come in as a senior. An awesome person, high basketball IQ and mother figure for everybody. You’ve got Kelyn as a freshman and Jayden (Scott). Both very talented with what they can do. Maria Serrano is getting there. Then adding Sophia Otten, a Division I athlete and knows how to win. She’s brought a different energy to our team." The Aces must navigate a lot of time away from campus The schedule was lower on the list of importance when considering the last three months. But with the season now in view, Evansville will be tested before conference play begins on Dec. 18. Most of that coming on the road. UE starts the 2026-27 season with five straight road games: DePaul, Lindenwood, No. 14 Kentucky, Eastern Illinois and IU Indy. The Aces also have a notable trip to No. 23 Illinois in December. Five opponents finished in the top 200 of last year's final NCAA NET ratings (UE plays home-and-home against Lindenwood). The MVC only published a top six preseason poll with two-time defending champion Murray State earning the top spot. The others were Illinois State, Belmont, Northern Iowa, Drake and UIC. The Aces open Valley play against three teams in that group – all on the road. "It’s a close-knit group," Wierzba said. "I think (the road schedule) just helps us to build those bonds. It’d be nice to have a home game sooner, but it’s part of it. What we’ve gone through, I think just being together is going to be huge for this team." Kyle Sokeland is a sports reporter for the Courier & Press. Follow him on X (formerly Twitter) @kylesokeland or email at kyle.sokeland@courierpress.com. item.title: Alyssa Volkers makes Hamilton history as first swimmer with state cuts in every event
item.description: Alyssa Volkers has proven to be one of the fastest and most versatile swimmers in West Michigan the past four years. But this season, she has proven to be the most versatile swimmer in Hamilton history. When Volkers won the 100-yard breaststroke in 1:13.76 on Thursday, Oct. 22, she became the first swimmer in Hamilton history to earn a state cut in all 11 swimming events in the same season. "I honestly never really thought about getting all the cuts until the day before when coach texted me and asked if I’d be willing to try for the last one in the 100 breaststroke, and I told her I would love to. It was actually my first time ever swimming the 100 breaststroke, so I was excited to try something new and see what I could do." More: Hamilton's Alyssa Volkers commits to swim at NCAA top 10 program Turns out she could do a lot. She won the race at Northview and earned a Division 3 state qualifying time. "I didn’t realize I was the first female swimmer from Hamilton to get all the state cuts in one season until the bus ride home, when AD Eric Talsma pointed it out," Volkers said. "At first, I thought it was just another fun accomplishment to add to my swimming journey and another thing to check off my list. But once I realized I was the first female swimmer from Hamilton to do it, I felt relieved and proud. It made me realize that all the hours, dedication, and hard work I’ve put into this sport have led to something bigger than what I initially expected. I didn’t come int Hamilton swimming excepting to make history, I just wanted to continue to improve in the sport I loved. Looking back, it's really special to know that something I worked toward for myself could also become a milestone for the program." She has state cuts in the 50, 100, 200 and 500 freestyle events, plus the 200 IM, 100 butterfly, 100 backstroke, 100 breaststroke and all three relays this season. Only a handful of swimmers in Holland-area history have accomplished the event. "To be able to earn eight individual state cuts in a single season is a huge deal," Hamilton coach Liz VanDeWege said. "It showcases her versatility as a swimmer in different distances and strokes even though she primarily trains distance. Alyssa's dedication and consistency day in and day out has proven time and time again that hard work pays off." That hard work is something Volkers enjoys. "I’ve put countless hours into the pool over the years, and it’s exciting to see that hard work pay off. Liz has changed Hamilton swimming a lot over the past year and has created sets around specific athletes, which has helped improve my swimming more than what I ever thought," Volkers said. "Swimming has become such a big part of my life that it’s almost muscle memory at this point. item.title: “Going To Ask What Serena Williams’ Doing” – Venus Williams Hints At What’s Next Amid Retirement Talks After Hong Kong Open Loss
item.description: Serena Williams and her sister, Venus Williams, compete in a doubles match during the Cincinnati Open at the Lindner Family Tennis Center in Mason on Aug. 17, 2026. The sisters fell to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns, 6-2, 1-6, 10-8. Venus Williams has hinted at her future in professional tennis. The former World No. 1 and seven-time Major singles champion continues to play despite suffering numerous chastening losses in recent seasons, particularly in singles. Her latest comments about her future came after a shocking first-round loss to 23-year-old compatriot Mary Stoiana, currently ranked outside the WTA top 100. On Monday, November 2, Stoiana delivered a dominant performance to defeat Williams 6-2, 6-3. After the result, which marked Williams’ 17th successive singles loss, the American tennis legend told AFP that she has yet to make concrete plans for her future in the sport. Currently ranked World No. 597 in singles, the 46-year-old said : “I haven’t made any plans for next year, also this year I didn’t make plans, just took it one step at a time.” She went on to mention her sister, Serena Williams, suggesting she could ‘copy’ the 23-time Grand Slam singles champion’s future plans. Williams added: “I’m going to ask what Serena Williams’ doing, probably copy her. We’ve always motivated each other. I’m really fully focused on every one week at a time, and whatever happens will happen, and I don’t have pressure to decide or anything.” Venus Williams’ most recent singles win came in Washington last year To find a singles win for Venus Williams, you have to go back to last year’s WTA 500 tournament in Washington. On that occasion, the former No. 1 delivered a stunning performance, beating compatriot Peyton Stearns 6-3, 6-4. The result made Williams the oldest match-winner on the WTA Tour since Martina Navratilova’s first-round win at the 2004 Wimbledon Championships. After her victory over Stearns, though, Williams has lost back-to-back matches against Magdalena Frech, Jessica Bouzas Maneiro, Karolina Muchova, Magda Linette, Tatjana Maria, Olga Danilovic, Ajla Tomljanovic, Diane Parry, Francesca Jones, Kaitlin Quevedo, Emiliana Arango, Kamilla Rakhimova, Anastasia Potapova, Irina-Camelia Begu, Sofia Kenin, Lilli Tagger, and most recently, Stoiana. Williams’ dismal run in singles has repeatedly prompted tennis fans to urge tournaments to stop giving the former World No. 1 main-draw wildcards. According to these fans, events would be better off giving the wildcards to younger players looking for opportunities to shine at WTA Tour-level tournaments. Several fans have also demanded Williams’ retirement, opining that she simply isn’t good enough anymore to compete on the WTA Tour. The 46-year-old American hasn’t fared much better in doubles either. Even though she has picked up victories in the category, her overall win-loss record in women’s doubles so far this year stands at 5-11 ahead of her first-round match partnering Xu Yifan in Hong Kong. item.title: What time is Rutgers football vs. Wisconsin? TV, prediction for Week 10
item.description: PISCATAWAY – Rutgers football coach Greg Schiano expressed more confidence after his team’s most recent loss that the Scarlet Knights are capable of winning again this season. They pushed Michigan before losing 28-21 to fall to 2-6 in what’s been a difficult, frustrating and disappointing season for Rutgers. The Scarlet Knights have only four games remaining, and at this point nothing is coming easily. Their next chance to pick up a win will come on Saturday, Nov. 7 when they play Wisconsin at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin - a place where the Scarlet Knights have never won previously. Maybe, just maybe, they find a way against a Badgers team that’s enduring struggles of its own. Wisconsin is coming off a blowout 30-0 loss to Iowa, and the Badgers’ second-best win this season – a 24-20 win over then-13 th ranked Penn State back in September – no longer looks quite as good with the Nittany Lions turning in a disappointing season. Although Wisconsin did beat USC convincingly on Oct. 24. The Badgers’ offense has been underwhelming, averaging 318.3 yards per game, which ranks 15 th in the Big Ten. Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph, who was benched against Iowa, is completing just 55.6 percent of his passes. But their defense has been better, allowing just 290.1 yards per game, good for seventh in the conference. So that unit will challenge the Scarlet Knights and quarterback AJ Surace, who completed just three passes (all in the first half) against Michigan. And it remains to be seen if star wide receiver KJ Duff, who left the loss to the Wolverines with an apparent lower-body injury, will play against Wisconsin. This will be another tough game in a tough environment for the Scarlet Knights. Rutgers football schedule: Scarlet Knights' next game Rutgers plays Wisconsin on Saturday, Nov. 7 at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin in their Week 10 game. What time is Rutgers vs. Wisconsin? Kickoff is scheduled for 4:15 ET. What channel is Rutgers vs. Wisconsin? The game will be televised on Big Ten Network. Watch Rutgers vs. Wisconsin live on Fubo (free trial for new subscribers) Rutgers vs. Wisconsin spread Rutgers is a 16.5-point underdog, according to Vegas Insider. Rutgers vs. Wisconsin prediction The Rutgers offense has been underwhelming because of the quarterback play without Dylan Lonergan. His status remains unclear – Schiano said after the Michigan loss that he’s not certain if Lonergan will return this season. Against a solid defense like Wisconsin’s, Surace is going to have his hands full. That’s especially true if Duff isn’t available. The Scarlet Knights’ defense has gotten better, and it should be able to limit a weak Badgers offense. Still, if Rutgers can’t stop Wisconsin on third down – an issue that hurt it badly against Michigan – this could be a long day for Travis Johansen’s unit. This will likely be a relatively low scoring game, but the Badgers pull out the win at home. Score prediction: Wisconsin 24, Rutgers 13

item.title: Top Section 4 field hockey players named New York all-state in field hockey
item.description: Whitney Point, Windsor, Vestal and Spencer-Van Etten/Candor reemerged as Section 4’s most dominant teams in girls’ field hockey, and Section 4 announced which star athletes had the biggest hand in this year’s success. Windsor, Vestal, and Whitney Point captured the Section 4 Class A, B, and C titles this season, with each school adding its fourth straight sectional title since 2023. The trio has rotated state championship status since 2014, with Whitney Point boasting the most state titles in Section 4 ( 11 ) and Windsor boasting a new dawn with its first-ever state title just last year. Five of the eight 2026 all-state selections were players from this year’s big three. Whitney Point seniors Ava Oliver, Kylan Smith and junior Anah Huston; Windsor senior Claire Beattie; and Vestal senior Elsa Hartman were named as all-state selections. 2026 All-State selections: Elsa Hartman, sr. Windsor, Vestal, and Whitney Point captured the Section 4 Class A, B, and C titles this season, with each school adding its fourth straight sectional title since 2023. The trio has rotated state championship status since 2014, with Whitney Point boasting the most state titles in Section 4 ( 11 ) and Windsor boasting a new dawn with its first-ever state title just last year. Five of the eight 2026 all-state selections were players from this year’s big three. item.title: Can Big Ten spending cap provide level playing field for Purdue football?
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE — Revenue sharing in college athletics is in its second year. For Purdue football it hasn't been the great equalizer that was anticipated. If indeed finances are what's limiting the Boilermakers from winning more games, the resolution comes in the Big Ten's adopted cap . Now, can Purdue get to that $49 million number to at least financially be at an equal playing field to its conference peers? It has been able to fully participate in revenue sharing . NIL income will be a tougher challenge, though some of Purdue's more marketable recent men's basketball players have received national brand endorsements while still in college. The Big Ten Conference, in anticipation of the Protect College Sports Act passing, announced on Oct. 28 that member schools can spend no more than $49 million, combining revenue sharing funds (allotted $21.58 million for the 2026-27 calendar year) and name, image and likeness (NIL) third-party deals. "Purdue has proven in our conversations in the last couple months that we are going to be aggressive and do everything that we can to give our sport teams the backing and the support and the resources that are necessary to be competitive in this conference and then nationally," Purdue football coach Barry Odom said. The $49 million can be distributed however athletic departments see fit, but $5 million must be allocated for women's and Olympic sports, falling in line with the PCSA. A majority of the remainder, likely at every Big Ten school, would be spent on football. More: Maryland serves as Purdue football's best, and maybe last, chance at victory According to a report published by The Athletic in September 2026, Purdue was estimated to have a $16-20 million roster. While other Big Ten programs rank in the same neighborhood estimate wise, the low end of Purdue's estimated roster cost would rank last in the league. Ohio State and Oregon both currently have estimated football rosters costing at or more than the $49 million cap. "When that number was floated around and then came out, I think some were really excited about it and some were disappointed about it because of the lack of equality in that world so to speak in the last couple of years," Odom said. As much as Odom wants to build a roster on high school recruiting and retention, that's not a fully realistic approach anymore. Nineteen players from Purdue's 2025 roster are currently playing college football elsewhere. Fifteen starters, and a punter, joined Purdue's roster since last year's season ended via the transfer portal. "The calendar is now sped up almost a year on not only identifying guys but then trying to attract that roster, plus a healthy high school recruiting database and footprint," Odom said. "And then the roster management piece of, OK, if you lose a couple of guys that are in their fourth year, really I don't want to replace them with incoming freshmen because of the maturity standpoint and proven over potential." item.content:encoded: WEST LAFAYETTE — Revenue sharing in college athletics is in its second year. For Purdue football it hasn't been the great equalizer that was anticipated. If indeed finances are what's limiting the Boilermakers from winning more games, the resolution comes in the Big Ten's adopted cap . Now, can Purdue get to that $49 million number to at least financially be at an equal playing field to its conference peers? It has been able to fully participate in revenue sharing . NIL income will be a tougher challenge, though some of Purdue's more marketable recent men's basketball players have received national brand endorsements while still in college. The Big Ten Conference, in anticipation of the Protect College Sports Act passing, announced on Oct. 28 that member schools can spend no more than $49 million, combining revenue sharing funds (allotted $21.58 million for the 2026-27 calendar year) and name, image and likeness (NIL) third-party deals. "Purdue has proven in our conversations in the last couple months that we are going to be aggressive and do everything that we can to give our sport teams the backing and the support and the resources that are necessary to be competitive in this conference and then nationally," Purdue football coach Barry Odom said. The $49 million can be distributed however athletic departments see fit, but $5 million must be allocated for women's and Olympic sports, falling in line with the PCSA. A majority of the remainder, likely at every Big Ten school, would be spent on football. More: Maryland serves as Purdue football's best, and maybe last, chance at victory According to a report published by The Athletic in September 2026, Purdue was estimated to have a $16-20 million roster. While other Big Ten programs rank in the same neighborhood estimate wise, the low end of Purdue's estimated roster cost would rank last in the league. Ohio State and Oregon both currently have estimated football rosters costing at or more than the $49 million cap. "When that number was floated around and then came out, I think some were really excited about it and some were disappointed about it because of the lack of equality in that world so to speak in the last couple of years," Odom said. As much as Odom wants to build a roster on high school recruiting and retention, that's not a fully realistic approach anymore. Nineteen players from Purdue's 2025 roster are currently playing college football elsewhere. Fifteen starters, and a punter, joined Purdue's roster since last year's season ended via the transfer portal. "The calendar is now sped up almost a year on not only identifying guys but then trying to attract that roster, plus a healthy high school recruiting database and footprint," Odom said. "And then the roster management piece of, OK, if you lose a couple of guys that are in their fourth year, really I don't want to replace them with incoming freshmen because of the maturity standpoint and proven over potential." The attraction part of Odom's statement gets more appealing if it is on a level playing field as the rest of the Big Ten and, if the PCSA passes, the rest of Power 4. Previously, there was undoubtedly players Purdue couldn't get its foot in the door with simply because of financials. Winning helps, too, which also has not been in Purdue's favor since the installments of revenue sharing and NIL. In 2025, despite a 2-10 record, Purdue just about maximized what was possible with its roster. That hasn't been the case this season for the Boilermakers, currently 3-5 and with a significant talent upgrade across the board from a season ago. While others in Purdue's money pool bracket, such as Iowa, have managed to find success doing more with less, it hasn't materialized through eight games for Purdue. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. Email him at sking@jconline.com and follow him on X and Instagram @samueltking. item.title: Israeli opposition unites behind Eisenkot as Netanyahu says voters chose him for PM
item.description: Israel's opposition is on Tuesday due to meet for the first time since last week's closely contested election in which neither Gadi Eisenkot's change bloc nor incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing alliance managed to win a majority in the Knesset. All parties in Eisenkot's camp have endorsed him to be the next prime minister, but the hot-button issue will be whether to unite with the Arab parties who made surprise gains in the vote.

item.title: How to watch Mizzou basketball vs Cleveland State. TV channel, streaming, tipoff
item.description: Hoops season is back in Columbia. Missouri basketball will open its 2026-27 season Tuesday, Nov. 3, with a game against Cleveland State at Mizzou Arena. Mizzou coach Dennis Gates previously coached the Vikings before taking over at Missouri . The Tigers are the first team ranked outside of the preseason AP Top 25 and the third team outside of the USA Today Sports Coaches Poll. Five-star freshmen Jason Crowe Jr. and Toni Bryant are expected to make their Mizzou debuts on Tuesday, and Mark Mitchell is eligible to play courtesy of an injunction against the NCAA. More: Guard CJ Gunn ruled ineligible, will not play for Missouri basketball this year More: Missouri basketball transfer forward suspended indefinitely Here’s how to watch Missouri play Cleveland State on Tuesday night: What channel is Missouri basketball’s game vs Cleveland State on? TV Channel: NA Stream: SEC Network+ (available via ESPN+) Missouri’s game against Cleveland State will stream live on SEC Network+, which is accessible with ESPN+. Nate Gatter will be the play-by-play announcer for the game, and Jarrett Sutton will be the on-air analyst and Taylor Kauffman will be the sideline reporter. The game will not air on a traditional cable network, but if your cable subscription has SEC Network included you can access SEC Network+ for free. Stream Mizzou basketball with ESPN+ What time will Missouri vs Cleveland State tip off? Date: Tuesday, Nov. 3 Time: 7 p.m. CT Location: Mizzou Arena in Columbia, Mo. Missouri’s game against Cleveland State will tip off at 7 p.m. CT Tuesday, Nov. 3, at Mizzou Arena. How to listen to Tuesday’s game Satellite radio: XM: 272; SXM App: 982 Tiger Radio Network will air the game live with ‘Voice of the Tigers’ Mike Kelly as the play-by-play announcer and Chris Gervino as the analyst on satellite channel 272. item.title: Meet the revamped Missouri State men's basketball roster
item.description: Missouri State’s new-look, men's basketball roster is ready to make its debut. The Bears will feature 12 new players from overseas, junior college and Division II ranks. Trey Williams Jr., Melakih Cunningham and Cameron Boone are the only three returning players from last year’s roster. The Bears host Division II Lincoln University for the season opener at 7 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 2. Here’s who will represent Missouri State this season, with comments from head coach Cuonzo Martin on each player. No. 1 Trey Williams Jr. Position: Guard Height: 6-3 Year: Sophomore Hometown : Centralia, Illinois Former school: Vashon Last year's stats: 9.4 points, 2.0 rebounds, 3.2 assists Martin's comments: "Trey has done a really good job leading. He's a point guard that can score the ball and also facilitate." Missouri State: Meet the 2026-27 women's basketball team No. 2 Kuol Kuol Position: Forward Height: 6-11 Year : Freshman Hometown : Abyei, South Sudan Former school: Oak Hill Academy Martin's comments: "Energy, run, spread the floor and is very active. High level motor." No. 3 Kevin Stubblefield Jr. Position: Guard Height: 6-5 Year : Junior Hometown : Omaha, Nebraska Former school: Westside High School, Connors State (Oklahoma junior college) Last year's stats: 19.1 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.8 assists with Connors State Martin's comments: "Good all-around basketball player. Reads the game and sees the game. He has a great feel for the game." item.title: West Ham sack Nuno Espírito Santo as head coach with club eighth in Championship
item.description: West Ham intent on instant return to Premier League Nuno took over from Graham Potter in September 2025 West Ham have sacked Nuno Espírito Santo after a disappointing run of form. The club kept faith with the head coach after last season’s relegation from the Premier League but patience has snapped with the side eighth in the Championship after last Saturday’s 3-1 defeat by West Bromwich Albion. Nuno struggled to get his ideas across after taking over from Graham Potter in September 2025. He had 33 games to save West Ham from relegation but his tactics were poor, his team selections were confusing and his signings have not worked out. Continue reading...

item.title: Apple warns of ‘unprecedented’ rise in memory chip prices
item.description: iPhone maker’s says decision to raise prices has offset some of impact, as revenues are stronger than expected Business live – latest updates Apple has warned of an “unprecedented” rise in memory chip prices, as it battles with datacentres to lay its hands on supplies. item.title: 'Avatar: Seven Havens' Season 2 Could Return to 'The Last Airbender’s Most Iconic Location
item.description: Ba Sing Se once survived a century-long war by pretending the war didn’t exist at all, only to get taken over by the Fire Nation during Avatar: The Last Airbender . Despite ongoing political turmoil extending through The Legend of Korra ’s era, the Earth Kingdom’s former capital persisted — and one version of it even survived the Cataclysm. Avatar: Seven Havens revealed the existence of a Haven called New Ba Sing Se during season 1, offering a glimpse of a society still clinging to old traditions while its people go hungry. And based on one specific detail from the season finale, there’s a very good reason to suspect we'll get to see the city of New Ba Sing Se firsthand in season 2.

item.title: Everyone has the file. Nobody has the right version
item.description: Distributed teams need to collaborate on shared information, but duplicated files, delays, and competing versions keep getting in the way. Picture a video production team with editors in different cities. One person updates a project file, another keeps working from an earlier copy, and a third waits for a large transfer to finish. When teams need to collaborate on large files across locations, traditional storage and file-sharing arrangements introduce friction precisely where people expect technology to help. Collaboration shouldn't require detective work The hard part isn't merely moving a file. It's knowing who has the authoritative copy, when changes are available, and whether somebody else is still working on an outdated version. Consider a game studio preparing a build for review. A designer exports an updated asset, but a colleague pulls an older version from a synced folder. The mistake only becomes obvious when the pieces are assembled. The team must trace the mismatch, resend files, and repeat work. Sync-and-download workflows depend on a chain of uploads, downloads, and decisions about which copy is current. Under deadline pressure, that chain breaks. Delayed access means missed handoffs; duplicated files mean extra checking and sometimes rework. For IT, each workaround creates another question: where does the data live, who can access it, and how do teams maintain consistent controls? Adding another collaboration application doesn't resolve those underlying questions. The useful starting point is the workflow. Find out where teams copy data, where they wait, and what prompts them to work outside the shared system. Compare notes with peers These frustrations cut across industries, but the ways organizations respond aren't identical. Hearing how another team handled version confusion, access, and handoffs is often more useful than another abstract promise of seamless collaboration. That's the focus of The Register and LucidLink’s invitation-only dinner on November 24 at Covent Garden Hotel in London. Joe Fay of The Register will moderate a peer discussion under the Chatham House Rule. Bring the real situations that never fit neatly into a technology diagram, and hear how others are handling them. item.title: NDC names Ibezi, Umeh, Nwoye to Anambra campaign council
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has appointed former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Ifeanyi Ibezi, as coordinator of its Anambra State campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections. The campaign council also features Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central; Senator Tony Nwoye, representing Anambra North; and Chief Ebuka Onunkwo, the party’s senatorial candidate for Anambra South. Other members include Emeka Kissinger Osisi as State Director of Youth Mobilisation, Barr. Ogechukwu Ekweozor as Director of Women Mobilisation, DIG Celestine Okoye (rtd) as Director of Security and AIG Innocent Ndubueze Anene (rtd) as Director of Election Monitoring and Vote Protection. The appointments were announced in a statement signed by the party’s State Director of Media and Publicity, Dr. Tony Onyima. The statement also named Chief Egwuoba Okika Innocent as Deputy State Coordinator, former Speaker of the Anambra State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Ikem Uzoezie, as State Chairman, and Barr. Paulinus Akabogu Izuchukwu as State Campaign Secretary. Campaign coordinators for the three senatorial districts are Hon. Kingsley Nwafor for Anambra South, Hon. Chuka Ezenwunne for Anambra Central and Hon. Chigbo Enwezor for Anambra North. All serving federal and state lawmakers elected on the party’s platform are also members of the campaign council. The council will operate through various directorates covering media and publicity, finance, logistics, women and youth mobilisation, security, grassroots mobilisation, election monitoring and vote protection, new media, protocol, policy research and documentation, and special duties. Onyima will serve as State Director of Media and Publicity, with Paschal Azubuike as his deputy, while Hon. Lady Azuka Enemuo and Mrs. Chika Ezeali will oversee finance as director and deputy director, respectively. The council also has coordinators for the 21 local government areas of the state as part of efforts to extend the party’s campaign activities to the grassroots. The NDC Anambra State Campaign Council is scheduled to be inaugurated on Wednesday, November 4, in Awka. The post NDC names Ibezi, Umeh, Nwoye to Anambra campaign council appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Soludo confirms Peter Obi’s wife as child’s godmother
item.description: Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has confirmed that the wife of former governor Peter Obi is the godmother of one of his children, months after a public disagreement over the relationship between their families. Soludo also disclosed that his wife, Nonye, is the confirmation godmother of Obi’s daughter, clarifying the family relationship that became a subject of public discussion in September. The governor made the disclosure in an interview with BBC News Igbo on Monday, describing Obi as a close friend and insisting that their families remained on good terms despite their political differences. “Peter Obi and I are good friends. Our two families are on good terms. His wife was the godmother of my child at baptism, and my wife was the godmother of his child at confirmation,” he said. Soludo explained that their differences were political, particularly over their preferences for who should govern Anambra State. He said he did not hold Obi’s political position against him, despite their disagreement over the state’s leadership. “I have a different vision of who should be governor of Anambra State. I am contesting, and he supported whoever he felt should be governor. I prevailed by the grace of God, and I don’t hold it against him,” the governor said. The post Soludo confirms Peter Obi’s wife as child’s godmother appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: African music legend, Youssou N’Dour, performing live at the Goalkeepers Dakar 2026. Photo by Seye Kehinde. On the 29th of October, 2026, Goalkeepers 2026 Dakar brought together global leaders, changemakers and young people to discuss how AI can help build a more equitable future. While the conversations explored the opportunities and challenges of using technology to advance progress, the event also made room for music and celebration. One of its special moments was a live performance by Senegalese music legend Youssou N’Dour , whose performance brought the audience to their feet. Youssou N’Dour is a Senegalese singer and politician who helped develop a style of popular Senegambian music known as mbalax that blends Wolof traditional instrumental and vocal forms primarily with Cuban and other Latin American popular genres. He also served as Senegal’s minister for culture and tourism. Watch the highlights of his performance below: It wouldn’t be a Dakar experience without some Youssou N’Dour! item.title: Forget retraining - AI can now tweak another AI's weights
item.description: The outputs of AI models are the result of a complex interplay between neurons, weights, training, and inference, and are therefore difficult to follow. But in some ways they're starting to look more like open books. Recent work by Anthropic safety fellow Joshua Fonseca Rivera has revealed how certain neurons in a neural network can be associated with a specific persona . Now, computer scientists from MIT's Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) have found that frontier AI models like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can rewrite the weights of another model directly, as opposed to indirectly through training, and alter their behavior. "We find early signs that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading, writing, and reasoning about neural network weights," said Rikiya Takehi, a PhD student at MIT CSAIL, in a social media post . "Instead of training, models may treat raw weights like readable, editable code: diagnosing failures and patching them directly." To demonstrate that, Takehi and colleagues Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab asked GPT-6 Astra to edit Qwen3.5-0.8B weights to make it better at math. Astra changed only 0.016 percent of the model's weights, reducing its reasoning loops and improving its math performance by as much as sixfold on the MATH-500 benchmark, while boosting its instruction-following score on the IFEval benchmark roughly threefold. There was no training using gradient descent ; Astra just revised the numerical values that constitute Qwen's weights. "All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops," the researchers wrote in a blog post . "It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming. "Throughout the history of deep learning, we encoded our simplistic inductive biases into tiny symbolic optimizers like Adam or Muon. This is changing: our neural network weights will soon be natively optimized by LLMs that deliberately reason about their weights." Astra's ability to program weights extends to being able to write a neural network from scratch, zero-shot. The researchers told Astra: "write, from scratch, the weights of a policy network that plays [Breakout] as well as possible." And it did so. Takehi suggests this technique shows promise for improving models without the consequences of catastrophic forgetting , which can occur when a model is revised to include new knowledge. More generally, the authors expect Weight-Space Programming will open the door to new ways to understand models and optimize them, and to implement recursive self-improvement. The technique may also prove useful for reducing model sycophancy and improving interpretability and alignment. item.title: Utomi faults APC over alleged extravagance amid hardship
item.description: Political economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration over what he described as extravagant lifestyles among public officials amid economic hardship in the country. Utomi said it was contradictory for government officials to describe Nigeria as poor while allegedly displaying luxury vehicles, including Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, and travelling in private jets. He made the remarks in a post on his X account on Tuesday, arguing that the lifestyles of public office holders should reflect the economic realities confronting ordinary Nigerians. “You cannot stand before the world and declare that Nigeria is poor, then turn around and parade your ministers in million-dollar Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, while public officials fly around in private jets. Your optics contradict your narrative, your lifestyle contradicts your statistics,” he said. The former presidential candidate said if Nigeria was indeed poor, government spending and the management of public resources should reflect the country’s economic circumstances. He argued that members of the executive and legislature should demonstrate fiscal restraint, particularly when citizens were being asked to endure economic difficulties. According to him, public office should not be treated as a licence for extravagance, adding that government officials had a responsibility to show restraint in the use of public resources. “The APC needs to understand that public office is not a licence for extravagance. If citizens must endure economic hardship, those entrusted with their taxes must also demonstrate restraint,” Utomi said. He added that displaying luxury lifestyles while asking Nigerians to endure economic hardship could deepen public resentment and reinforce perceptions that government officials were insensitive to the plight of ordinary citizens. The post Utomi faults APC over alleged extravagance amid hardship appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu Stepped In When Nigeria Was About To Collapse — Mutfwang
item.description: Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has called on Nigerians to exercise patience with President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the President inherited a country burdened by longstanding fiscal and structural challenges, and about to collapse when he assumed office in 2023. Mutfwang argued that the economic difficulties confronting the country did not begin with the Tinubu administration, insisting that Nigerians must consider the state of the economy at the time the President took over before assessing the impact of the ongoing reforms. The Governor stated this on Monday while inaugurating the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections at the Government House, Rayfield, Jos. Mutfwang Inaugurates 2027 APC Campaign Council He acknowledged the hardship occasioned by the economic adjustments but maintained that the reforms were necessary to address deep-rooted challenges, pointing to improvements in the country’s foreign reserves and fuel availability as indications of progress. Mutfwang urged Nigerians to give the reforms time to yield results, stressing that the country’s economic recovery required sustained commitment and an understanding of the challenges inherited by the present administration. “Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria tottering on the brink of collapse; Nigeria that could not service its external debts; Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home. And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria because they could not get the dollars to take back their money. “Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades. Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” the governor said. The inauguration marked the commencement of coordinated mobilisation for the re-election of President Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima, as well as Governor Mutfwang, Deputy Governor Josephine Piyo and other APC candidates contesting National and State Assembly seats in Plateau State. item.content:encoded: Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has called on Nigerians to exercise patience with President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the President inherited a country burdened by longstanding fiscal and structural challenges, and about to collapse when he assumed office in 2023. Mutfwang argued that the economic difficulties confronting the country did not begin with the Tinubu administration, insisting that Nigerians must consider the state of the economy at the time the President took over before assessing the impact of the ongoing reforms. The Governor stated this on Monday while inaugurating the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections at the Government House, Rayfield, Jos. Mutfwang Inaugurates 2027 APC Campaign Council He acknowledged the hardship occasioned by the economic adjustments but maintained that the reforms were necessary to address deep-rooted challenges, pointing to improvements in the country’s foreign reserves and fuel availability as indications of progress. Mutfwang urged Nigerians to give the reforms time to yield results, stressing that the country’s economic recovery required sustained commitment and an understanding of the challenges inherited by the present administration. “Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria tottering on the brink of collapse; Nigeria that could not service its external debts; Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home. And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria because they could not get the dollars to take back their money. “Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades. Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” the governor said. The inauguration marked the commencement of coordinated mobilisation for the re-election of President Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima, as well as Governor Mutfwang, Deputy Governor Josephine Piyo and other APC candidates contesting National and State Assembly seats in Plateau State. The Governor also highlighted measures taken by his administration to ease the economic burden on residents, including the introduction of Tin City Metro buses, revival of rail services within Jos metropolis, a 50 per cent reduction in tuition fees in state-owned tertiary institutions and a 300 per cent increase in student allowances. He further acknowledged the benefits of the Federal Government’s student loan and scholarship interventions, which he said had supported Plateau indigenes studying in various universities. On security, Mutfwang admitted that challenges persisted across Plateau State but assured residents that his administration remained committed to protecting lives and property. He disclosed that plans were underway to facilitate the return of internally displaced persons to their ancestral communities, with another batch of retrained Operation Rainbow personnel and at least 800 trained forest guards expected to be deployed in vulnerable areas in the coming weeks. Making a case for his administration’s second term, the Governor said governance was a continuous process, noting that his government needed another opportunity to consolidate ongoing projects and programmes. “There is no government that ends everything. Every government is a relay. Our duty is not to make others look bad; it is to see how we can collectively make Plateau State look better,” he said. He charged members of the campaign council to take the APC’s message to every community, emphasising that electoral success depended on effective grassroots mobilisation. “The votes are in the polling unit. They are not in Jos. Everybody can only matter in the locality where you come from,” Mutfwang stated. Earlier, the Director-General of the Mutfwang/Piyo 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, Sir Joseph Ari, pledged that the campaign would be factual, issue-based and peaceful, without bitterness or acrimony. Ari disclosed that the council had received expressions of support from 115 support groups, alongside solidarity visits and assurances from traditional rulers, religious leaders, women, youths and other organised groups. He said the council would rely on teamwork, strategic coordination and inclusive engagement to communicate its message across the state. The Plateau State APC Chairman, Rufus Bature, described the inauguration as a significant step towards building a coordinated campaign structure, urging members to strengthen the party’s grassroots organisation and remain committed to their responsibilities. Ari also called on party faithful and residents to turn out on November 14, 2026, to welcome President Tinubu, Vice President Shettima, APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, and other national party leaders during their scheduled visit to Plateau State. item.title: Police rescue 11 kidnapped victims, arrest 19 suspects
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has rescued 11 kidnapped victims, arrested 19 suspects and recovered 91 rustled livestock, including 48 cows and 43 sheep, in security operations conducted across several states in the last 48 hours. The operations also led to the recovery of firearms, stolen valuables and motorcycles, while several attempted bandit attacks were foiled. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, disclosed the operational breakthroughs in a statement on Tuesday, saying the operations were part of sustained efforts to combat kidnapping, terrorism, armed robbery, cultism, cattle rustling and other criminal activities. He said investigations and follow-up operations were ongoing to apprehend fleeing suspects, rescue more victims and recover stolen property. In Zamfara State, police tactical operatives, working with local vigilantes, rescued five elderly women abducted by armed bandits while harvesting beans in Dansadau, Maru Local Government Area. The victims were freed following a gun battle that forced the abductors to flee. However, a 35-year-old farmer was killed during the attack. In Niger State, a joint security team comprising police, military personnel, Department of State Services operatives, special hunters and vigilantes rescued six farmers abducted at Mahangi village, near Pandogari in Rafi Local Government Area. The victims were subsequently taken to a police division for documentation and reunion with their families. In Kebbi State, joint security forces repelled an attack by suspected Lakurawa terrorists on Ribah town in Danko Wasagu Local Government Area on October 30, after the attackers attempted to block Rambo Junction. The operation followed an earlier attack on Dan-Indo village in Fakai Local Government Area, where nine people were killed, while two vehicles and several motorcycles were set ablaze. The police said security operatives had been deployed to maintain order and sustain operations against the suspected terrorists. Also in Zamfara, police and soldiers have launched a coordinated search-and-rescue operation following the abduction of nine persons at Upa, near Kurya Madaro in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area. Bush-combing operations are ongoing in surrounding forests to secure their release and apprehend the perpetrators. item.content:encoded: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has rescued 11 kidnapped victims, arrested 19 suspects and recovered 91 rustled livestock, including 48 cows and 43 sheep, in security operations conducted across several states in the last 48 hours. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, disclosed the operational breakthroughs in a statement on Tuesday, saying the operations were part of sustained efforts to combat kidnapping, terrorism, armed robbery, cultism, cattle rustling and other criminal activities. In Zamfara State, police tactical operatives, working with local vigilantes, rescued five elderly women abducted by armed bandits while harvesting beans in Dansadau, Maru Local Government Area. The victims were freed following a gun battle that forced the abductors to flee. However, a 35-year-old farmer was killed during the attack. In Niger State, a joint security team comprising police, military personnel, Department of State Services operatives, special hunters and vigilantes rescued six farmers abducted at Mahangi village, near Pandogari in Rafi Local Government Area. The victims were subsequently taken to a police division for documentation and reunion with their families. In Kebbi State, joint security forces repelled an attack by suspected Lakurawa terrorists on Ribah town in Danko Wasagu Local Government Area on October 30, after the attackers attempted to block Rambo Junction. The operation followed an earlier attack on Dan-Indo village in Fakai Local Government Area, where nine people were killed, while two vehicles and several motorcycles were set ablaze. The police said security operatives had been deployed to maintain order and sustain operations against the suspected terrorists. Also in Zamfara, police and soldiers have launched a coordinated search-and-rescue operation following the abduction of nine persons at Upa, near Kurya Madaro in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area. Bush-combing operations are ongoing in surrounding forests to secure their release and apprehend the perpetrators. In Kano State, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad arrested five suspects accused of harbouring criminals in connection with the abduction of the APC Chairman of Rogo Local Government Area, Alhaji Abdu Fanka. Although the principal suspects reportedly escaped, the police recovered 48 cows, 43 sheep and two Bajaj Boxer motorcycles from the location. In Katsina State, tactical teams foiled an attempted bandit attack on Karofi village in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area after responding to a distress call. The gunmen reportedly retreated into the bush following an exchange of gunfire. No casualty was recorded. In Lagos State, police arrested a 28-year-old suspected cultist, Ojo/Ojomu Bolanle, also known as Burna, in connection with an armed robbery at Desa Bus Stop, Ibeju-Lekki, which resulted in the killing of a Point-of-Sale operator, Ibrahim Adewale Moronfade. Items recovered from the suspect included a locally made pistol, an expended cartridge and charms. In Benue State, two suspects were arrested over the alleged sexual assault of a 16-year-old girl in Naka, Gwer West Local Government Area. The police said a medical examination conducted at General Hospital, Naka, confirmed penetration, while efforts were ongoing to apprehend the principal suspect, who was still at large. In the Federal Capital Territory, two suspects, Mensur Abdullahi, 20, and Gambo Salisu, 30, were arrested following a violent clash in Gwagwalada over a stolen Tecno phone. A 19-year-old passer-by, Zaharadenu Awalu, who sustained a deep cut on his left hand during the incident, was treated at the University of Abuja Teaching Hospital. The police said other suspects were being trailed. In Anambra State, two persons were arrested over the death of a man allegedly tortured and detained overnight by vigilante members at Odorober, Odekpe, over an allegation of stealing a vehicle battery. In Oyo State, police arrested a 30-year-old suspected cattle rustler, Yali Isiya, following a gun duel between a police-vigilante patrol team and a four-man gang along the Maya-Adekola village axis in Lanlate. A vigilante member sustained injuries during the encounter and was taken to hospital, while other members of the gang escaped. In a separate incident in Ogbomoso, three students were arrested following an alleged invasion of Methodist Grammar School by students armed with cutlasses, knives and stones. One student was injured, while solar panels and classroom roofing materials valued at about N500,000 were reportedly damaged. Police recovered two cutlasses, a catapult and stones. In Ogun State, two suspected burglars, Bidemi Akinola, 23, and Qudus Adebayo, 22, were arrested over a burglary at Igbehinadun Street. The suspects allegedly confessed to stealing property valued at N4.085 million, including a 55-inch television, air conditioners, generators and electrical wires. Tools and stolen cables were also recovered. Meanwhile, in the FCT, police patrol teams responded to an attack by suspected cattle rustlers on a Fulani settlement in Phase 5, Kurudu, on October 30. Four persons sustained gunshot injuries and were taken to Nyanya General Hospital. Three were treated and discharged, while the fourth victim died. The Force reiterated its commitment to intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local communities to curb criminal activities and improve public safety nationwide. item.title: 2027: Atiku’s presidency won’t determine Senate President, Reps Speaker — Melaye
item.description: The Deputy Director-General of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dino Melaye, has said a government led by Atiku Abubakar will not determine who becomes Senate President or Speaker of the House of Representatives. Melaye said the ADC would allow lawmakers to elect their leaders independently, insisting that the party was committed to democratic principles and an independent National Assembly. He stated this while answering questions on the oversight mechanisms the ADC would introduce to track government payments, fund releases and beneficiaries during an appearance on Arise Television’s Prime Time on Monday. “To start with, an Atiku presidency will not determine who is going to be the Senate president, the president of the Senate, or the Speaker of the House of Representatives,” he said. “Atiku is a Democrat. ADC is a very democratic political party. So we are going to allow the people to elect their leaders.” Melaye argued that allowing lawmakers to choose their leaders would promote legislative independence and strengthen the National Assembly’s oversight of the executive arm of government. “And I told you that wherever you have the members electing their leaders, there is some modicum of independence,” he said. “So to start with, the ADC will make sure that the National Assembly is truly independent, and if the National Assembly is truly independent, that will drive their oversight functions over the Executive.” On the mechanisms for scrutinising government spending, the ADC campaign official said relevant National Assembly committees would be empowered to question government officials and monitor expenditure. He specifically identified the Committees on Establishment, Finance, and Budget and Planning as possible channels for investigating government spending and ensuring accountability. “The Committee on Establishment is responsible for questioning this type of spenders because they have direct oversight function over the State House. The committee on finance is there. The committee on budget and planning is there,” Melaye said. “So you can use any of these committees at least to ask questions.” The post 2027: Atiku’s presidency won’t determine Senate President, Reps Speaker — Melaye appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 'The Mandalorian' Meets 'Avatar' in Netflix's New Sci-Fi Western Masterpiece
item.description: Created by LeSean Thomas and Studio Mir, who both worked on The Legend of Korra , Bass X Machina is a reimagining of the story of Bass Reeves (Brian Tyree Henry), an escaped slave who worked in Indian Territory as a deputy U.S. Marshal. Reeves’ real life was extraordinary, and is said to have inspired the character of the Lone Ranger, but Bass X Machina also gives him a cybernetic arm that shoots magic bullets. The criminals he fights get even bigger upgrades, and the stakes can at times escalate to truly ludicrous levels. Henry does an especially great job expressing exasperation as Bass faces plenty of absurd foes, like an outlaw in a rampaging bull mech that requires complex cooperation to take down.

item.title: Atiku faults Cross River security over alleged estate robberies
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has criticised the security arrangements around Cross River State Governor’s private residence in Calabar, following reports of alleged robberies in neighbouring homes. Atiku said residents of the estate where Governor Bassey Otu’s private residence is located had complained of repeated burglaries despite the presence of armed policemen and two roadblocks securing the governor’s property. According to him, one resident reportedly lost an air conditioner and a freezer to burglars, while another disclosed that two houses on a nearby street were attacked last week. The former Vice President disclosed this in a post on his X account on Tuesday, questioning the disparity between the security provided for the governor and the protection available to residents living in the same neighbourhood. He said the governor had been operating from his private residence for nearly three years while the Government House was undergoing renovation, yet residents living nearby remained exposed to security threats. “This is security, APC style: two roadblocks for the governor, and none for the people next door,” Atiku said. He questioned the capacity of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to address insecurity across the state, asking what it could offer communities outside the state capital if residents living beside the governor could not sleep without fear. Atiku also outlined his proposed security reforms, pledging to transform the Nigeria Police Force from what he described as a regime-protecting force into a citizen-focused public service. He said his administration would expand police personnel towards the international benchmark of one officer to every 450 citizens to improve security coverage across communities. The ADC presidential candidate also promised to establish community-based security and intelligence networks to enable neighbourhoods to identify and report threats before criminal activities occur. “Security that stops at the governor’s gate is not security; it is a fence,” he added. The post Atiku faults Cross River security over alleged estate robberies appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US Strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island — Report
item.description: The United States on Monday attacked Iran’s Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported, even as President Donald Trump signaled progress in negotiations with Tehran to end the eight-month-old conflict. The Journal, citing unnamed US officials, described the strike against Qeshm, the largest island in the Strait of Hormuz, as the latest of a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out against Iran in recent weeks. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession were heard on the island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies. The Pentagon referred questions about the reported strikes to US Central Command, which did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment late Monday. The Journal reported that the US has been engaged in smaller-scale strikes against Iran for several weeks. It said some officials described the assaults as defensive in nature to prevent Iran from having the freedom to attack commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, a key conduit for oil shipments that has been largely blocked since the war began in late February. This picture taken by the southern Lebanese village of Zawtar al-Garbiya shows an Israeli excavator demolishing homes in the town of Zawtar al-Sharqiya on November 2, 2026. The paper said the US has not publicly announced the attacks, so as not to signal any intention of resuming major combat operations. On Monday, on the eve of midterm elections in the United States, Trump said that a deal with Tehran “could happen.” Oil prices, sent rocketing by Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz energy corridor, plunged by more than seven percent on Monday on optimism over a possible end to the conflict. AFP The post US Strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island — Report appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Don’t call it a remontada: Emery’s Camp Nou comeback focuses European blur
item.description: The expanded Champions League is often shapeless, but Aston Villa’s manager returning to the scene of his greatest trauma stands out “One more match. Just one more match.” Sure, Unai. Sure. Just like all the other matches that generated a local tremor measured at 1 on the Richter scale when that seventh and final goal went in at the Camp Nou in March 2017. It was inevitable that Unai Emery would be asked about the Remontada game on the eve of Aston Villa’s Champions League engagement with Barcelona, his own first trip back to the Camp Nou in this competition since one of the most visceral and traumatic experiences of his managerial career. Continue reading...

item.title: AFC postpones Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia to late 2027 due to conflict in Middle East
item.description: Tournament pushed back 11 months with proposed start on 23 December New dates with 21 January 2028 final must be approved by Fifa The 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia has been postponed as a result of the conflict in the Middle East. After a month of speculation following the airport attack on Riyadh’s international airport, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) confirmed on Tuesday that the tournament had been pushed back 11 months. item.title: How the New Tax Stamp Could Show Up in Everyday Life
item.description: We’ve all been there: planning a weekend dinner with friends, throwing a birthday bash, or just kicking back at home with a few favourite treats. Drinks and refreshments are basically a staple of these moments. But have you ever stopped to think about how behind-the-scenes government policies end up changing the price tags on those items? With the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) rolling out its new excise stamp policy in January 2026, that question is at the forefront, especially for brands that make things like alcohol, tobacco, and sugar-sweetened beverages. Honestly, nobody’s really stressing over the policy itself. What people care about is the ripple effect: how companies handle the new regulation and whether those adjustments will make our favourite items more expensive on the shelf. When Business Meets Your Wallet Behind every product is a mountain of decisions from packaging and distribution to compliance and production. Most of the time, we never see this happening, but it plays a huge role in how items are priced. When new regulations bring extra costs, companies find themselves at a crossroads. Some choose to absorb the blow internally to keep customers happy, while others might tweak their prices. It really comes down to the specific brand, the market, and how heavy the financial lift is. For everyday shoppers, that’s usually the moment a boring policy talk suddenly feels very real. What Does This Mean for How We Spend ? The change probably won’t hit overnight, and it might not even be dramatic. But over time, small shifts in everyday prices can change how we shop. You might find yourself comparing brands a bit more closely, hunting for promos and discounts, or rethinking how much cash you drop on certain treats. Brands, meanwhile, are caught in a tricky balancing act: keeping loyal customers without going broke on rising operating costs. Just keep in mind: a new tax stamp doesn’t automatically mean prices are shooting up. It all depends on how companies adapt and whether those extra costs trickle down to us. The Bigger Picture At the end of the day, this is really about finding a middle ground. The government wants solid systems to collect taxes, while businesses need a framework that lets them stay afloat and grow. But come to think of it, the authorities are already equipped with internal tracking solutions, such as electronic invoicing from FIRS alongside the Customs Service’s B’Odogwu digital excise register, rendering physical paper tags largely redundant. Striking that balance matters because business decisions don’t just stay on a spreadsheet. They shape the things we buy, the choices we make, and how we manage our money. Right now, it’s still a bit early to tell what the full impact on consumers will be. But staying clued in on what’s driving the market makes it a whole lot easier to navigate the changes coming our way. item.title: WARRI DELINEATION: Lawyer seeks probe, warns against political manipulation, violence
item.description: Lawyer and politician, Chief Robinson Ariyo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to investigate the Warri delineation exercise, saying there are allegations of financial inducement to favour some areas over others. Ariyo also called on the President to direct the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice to provide an independent written legal opinion on the legality of the exercise. In a statement, he urged the President to direct relevant agencies to preserve all documents and records relating to the exercise and investigate allegations of financial misconduct, security compromises and electoral irregularities. He further called for an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly those whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records might be connected to the allegations surrounding the Warri delineation controversy. Ariyo also urged the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, ICPC, and Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit, NFIU, to investigate credible allegations of suspicious dollar transactions, unexplained financial inflows and possible financial inducement of political actors, public officers, electoral personnel and security operatives in connection with the controversy. The statement reads: “That the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice be requested to provide an independent, written legal opinion on the legality of the ongoing Warri delineation exercise, identifying the applicable constitutional provisions, statutory powers, judicial orders and procedural requirements governing the exercise. The opinion should specifically distinguish between the delineation of electoral wards, State Constituencies and Federal Constituencies. “That INEC be formally requested, in the exercise of its constitutional independence, to publish the complete delineation report, supporting maps, methodology, relevant population and geographical data, stakeholder submissions and reasons for accepting or rejecting material objections. That the Commission be urged to undertake a transparent review of any substantiated procedural or factual irregularities and refrain from implementing any aspect found to be unlawful, subject always to applicable judicial orders and statutory requirements. “That all relevant documents, correspondence, meeting records, maps, electronic records, financial documents and administrative communications relating to the exercise be preserved against destruction, alteration or concealment. “That the appropriate federal authorities undertake an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly contracts whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records may be relevant to the allegations raised herein. item.dc:creator: Urowayino Jeremiah
item.content:encoded: Lawyer and politician, Chief Robinson Ariyo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to investigate the Warri delineation exercise, saying there are allegations of financial inducement to favour some areas over others. Ariyo also called on the President to direct the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice to provide an independent written legal opinion on the legality of the exercise. In a statement, he urged the President to direct relevant agencies to preserve all documents and records relating to the exercise and investigate allegations of financial misconduct, security compromises and electoral irregularities. He further called for an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly those whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records might be connected to the allegations surrounding the Warri delineation controversy. Ariyo also urged the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, ICPC, and Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit, NFIU, to investigate credible allegations of suspicious dollar transactions, unexplained financial inflows and possible financial inducement of political actors, public officers, electoral personnel and security operatives in connection with the controversy. The statement reads: “That the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice be requested to provide an independent, written legal opinion on the legality of the ongoing Warri delineation exercise, identifying the applicable constitutional provisions, statutory powers, judicial orders and procedural requirements governing the exercise. The opinion should specifically distinguish between the delineation of electoral wards, State Constituencies and Federal Constituencies. “That INEC be formally requested, in the exercise of its constitutional independence, to publish the complete delineation report, supporting maps, methodology, relevant population and geographical data, stakeholder submissions and reasons for accepting or rejecting material objections. That the Commission be urged to undertake a transparent review of any substantiated procedural or factual irregularities and refrain from implementing any aspect found to be unlawful, subject always to applicable judicial orders and statutory requirements. “That all relevant documents, correspondence, meeting records, maps, electronic records, financial documents and administrative communications relating to the exercise be preserved against destruction, alteration or concealment. “That the appropriate federal authorities undertake an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly contracts whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records may be relevant to the allegations raised herein. The audit should cover contract awards, disbursements, beneficial ownership, subcontracting arrangements, foreign-currency transactions and evidence of possible diversion of public funds, an independent scrutiny and examination of the oil production and sales by the NNPC within the period in view to determine whether or not there are leakages and if there are, the extent of such leakages. “That the EFCC, ICPC, and NFIU, within their respective statutory mandates, investigate credible allegations of suspicious dollar transactions, unexplained financial inflows, and possible financial inducement of political actors, public officers, electoral personnel, or security operatives in connection with the Warri delineation controversy. “That the National Security Adviser, in collaboration with the relevant security agencies, conduct an impartial assessment of possible security compromises, threats to lives and property, and any evidence of inducement or improper influence involving security operatives in the affected areas. “That adequate and impartial security measures be maintained in Warri North, Warri South and Warri South-West Local Government Areas to protect all residents, traditional institutions and legitimate community interests, irrespective of ethnic affiliation. “That Your Excellency convene a genuinely inclusive stakeholder engagement involving recognised traditional rulers, community representatives, relevant political stakeholders, legal practitioners and other affected interests from the Itsekiri, Ijaw and Urhobo communities. Such engagement must not be used to impose a predetermined outcome but should provide an opportunity for all parties to present their grievances and supporting evidence. “That persons who provide credible information concerning financial misconduct, security compromise or electoral irregularities be afforded appropriate protection against intimidation, harassment, victimisation or retaliation. “That the appropriate agencies be directed to provide an initial report of their findings and recommendations within a reasonable and publicly communicated timeframe, subject to the requirements of confidentiality and due process. “Your Excellency, history will not merely remember the number of infrastructure projects executed or the economic policies implemented during an administration. It will also remember how that administration protected the Constitution, defended democratic institutions, and responded to credible allegations of abuse of public power. “The Niger Delta has contributed immeasurably to our country’s economic survival. Its people deserve fairness, justice, security and equitable political representation. The Warri delineation controversy must not become another chapter in the history of avoidable communal antagonism, political manipulation and institutional distrust. It would be deeply unfortunate if an exercise intended to improve electoral representation were to become a source of division, suspicion and possible violence. I respectfully remind Your Excellency that the Constitution is supreme and binding on all authorities and persons under Section 1(1) and (3) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended). “To demonstrate how unambiguous the governing provisions of the Constitution on the subject matter are, I humbly reproduce it as follows: Section 115: Time when alteration of State Constituencies takes effect. Where the boundaries of any State constituency established under section 112 of this Constitution are altered in accordance with the provisions of section 114 of this Constitution, that alteration shall come into effect after it has been approved by the National Assembly and after the current life of the House of Assembly”. “The issue is whether, having regard to the combined provisions of Sections 112, 113, 114 and 115 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) possesses the power to bring into effect an alteration of the boundaries of an existing State Constituency without the requisite approval of the National Assembly and before the expiration of the current life of the relevant State House of Assembly.” The post WARRI DELINEATION: Lawyer seeks probe, warns against political manipulation, violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NIMC arrests illegal NIN operators, seizes enrolment equipment
item.description: By Emmanuel Elebeke The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) has intensified its crackdown on illegal National Identification Number (NIN) enrolment, unauthorised data modification and extortion, following an enforcement operation that led to several arrests in Gwagwalada and other locations. The Commission disclosed this in a statement, saying its Inspectorate Compliance and Enforcement Unit (ICEU) carried out the operation and seized equipment allegedly used for illegal enrolment activities. It said the exercise was part of efforts to curb unauthorised enrolment and unethical practices while protecting the integrity, security and credibility of Nigeria’s National Identity Management System. NIMC noted that many of the challenges encountered by NIN holders resulted from attempts to bypass official enrolment procedures. It stressed that NIN enrolment could only be conducted at its approved centres, while requests for modification of personal data could be processed through its self-service modification platform. The Commission also advised NIN holders to download the NINAuth application from the iOS App Store or Google Play Store to access security features, print their NIN slips and enjoy other related services. The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of NIMC, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote, reiterated the Commission’s zero tolerance for extortion and unethical practices. She said the Commission remained committed to providing seamless and hitch-free NIN enrolment services for Nigerians and legal residents. NIMC urged applicants and existing NIN holders to use only its approved channels for enrolment and other related services. It advised members of the public to visit www.nimc.gov.ng or follow its verified social media platforms for accurate information. The post NIMC arrests illegal NIN operators, seizes enrolment equipment appeared first on Vanguard News .
